/** The attempt file, alongside `devices/`, `nonces/` and `audit/`. */
export const ATTEMPT_STORE_FILENAME = "answer-attempts.json";

/** Bumped ONLY for an incompatible shape change; an unknown version is quarantined. */
const ATTEMPT_FILE_VERSION = 1;

const ATTEMPT_FILE_MODE = 0o600;

/**
 * The only failure codes an attempt record may carry.
 *
 * `handleAnswer` writes exactly these two. The TYPE (`AttemptFailureCode`, in
 * `types.ts`) is what actually stops a third one being written: every record is
 * built as an `AnswerAttemptRecord`, so a code that is not in that union does not
 * compile, and this list and that union have to be widened together. This runtime
 * list is the disk boundary's copy of the same rule — one unrecognised code fails
 * the whole-file schema below and the whole file is then quarantined, so a single
 * mislabelled record would cost every other record's 24 h of coverage.
 *
 * `satisfies` ties the list to the type; the type ties it to `ErrorCode`.
 */
const ATTEMPT_FAILURE_CODES = [
	"guard_failed",
	"internal",
] as const satisfies readonly AttemptFailureCode[];

/**
 * A record whose shape this build cannot store — a PROGRAMMER error, not an I/O
 * failure, and separated from one so it cannot be swallowed as if it were.
 *
 * `recordOutcome` deliberately logs-and-continues when the disk write fails
 * (reporting a landed answer as failed is worse than an undurable record). That
 * tolerance must not extend to "this record can never be stored at all": a
 * `failureCode` outside `ATTEMPT_FAILURE_CODES` is thrown BEFORE the record
 * reaches memory, so swallowing it would leave the request's `in_flight` record
 * in place with nothing left to advance it — a permanent "still being typed" for
 * an attempt that finished. Distinguished by class and rethrown.
 */
export class AttemptRecordShapeError extends Error {}

const attemptGuardNameSchema = z.enum(
	Object.keys(GUARD_CLASSES) as [AnswerGuardName, ...AnswerGuardName[]],
);

/**
 * The on-disk record, validated at the disk boundary exactly as a wire body is
 * validated at the HTTP boundary. Nothing here is trusted because it came from
 * our own directory.
 */
const attemptRecordSchema = z.object({
	requestId: z.string().min(1).max(64),
	questionId: z.string().min(1).max(64),
	deviceId: z.string().min(1).max(64),
	surface: z.enum(["phone", "watch"]),
	leaseId: z.string().min(1).max(64),
	startedAtMs: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
	status: z.enum(["confirmed", "failed", "unconfirmed", "in_flight"]),
	resolvedAtMs: z.number().int().nonnegative().nullable(),
	failureCode: z.enum(ATTEMPT_FAILURE_CODES).nullable(),
	guardsPassed: z.array(attemptGuardNameSchema),
});

const attemptFileSchema = z.object({
	version: z.literal(ATTEMPT_FILE_VERSION),
	/**
	 * When this store first began recording, preserved across every rewrite.
	 *
	 * DIAGNOSTIC, not load-bearing: `recordsSinceMs` no longer derives the
	 * published coverage window from it, because a file that a lost rename rolled
	 * back carries this stamp UNCHANGED and would assert over the very records the
	 * rollback removed. It is kept because it is the install-time fact a future
	 * rise-only witness (the treatment `state-anchor.json` already has) would need
	 * in order to make pre-restart coverage provable again.
	 */
	coverageSinceMs: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
	records: z.array(attemptRecordSchema),
});

/**
 * §11.4/§11.5 — the 24 h idempotency + status record, keyed by `requestId`.
 * A replay returns the RECORDED outcome; a status read reports it.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * IT IS ON DISK, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * This used to be a bare `Map` built in `start()`. §11.5 says two things a
 * process-lifetime map cannot honour: records are retained for 24 HOURS, and
 * `known: false` is an ASSERTION THAT NOTHING WAS SENT which has to be true
 * whenever it is made. The bridge deliberately dies with the desktop app, which
 * this fork restarts often, so after every restart every earlier `requestId`
 * came back `known: false` — and the client turns that into a TERMINAL
 * "the desktop never saw this request — it was not sent". For an answer that
 * actually landed, that sends the user to re-answer a picker at the desk, which
 * §11.4 records as unrecoverable. `(ANSWER-INFLIGHT)` closed the ~15 s
 * pre-injection window and left this much larger one open, with a worse message.
 *
 * So: `tmp -> fsync -> rename` on every write (`writeFileDurable`, the same
 * discipline the §3.5 replay cache uses), hydrated at start, and a `put` that
 * does not resolve until the record is durable. `handleAnswer` awaits the
 * `in_flight` put BEFORE it takes the terminal lock, so any attempt that could
 * possibly have written a byte has a durable record first — which is what makes
 * `recordsSinceMs` a real guarantee rather than a hope.
 */
export interface AttemptStore {
	get(requestId: RequestId): AnswerAttemptRecord | null;
	/**
	 * Records in memory AND on disk. Resolves only once the record is durable;
	 * rejects if it could not be made durable, so the caller decides what an
	 * unrecordable attempt means (before the lock: refuse; after it: log, because
	 * a landed write must never be reported as failed).
	 */
	put(record: AnswerAttemptRecord): Promise<void>;
	/**
	 * Undoes a `put` whose durable write REJECTED, for a caller that is about to
	 * tell the client nothing was written.
	 *
	 * `put` records in memory before it persists, because the post-lock caller
	 * MUST keep an accurate in-memory outcome even when the disk write fails — a
	 * landed answer that read back as unsent is the exact lie this store exists to
	 * remove. The pre-lock caller needs the opposite: its 503 says "nothing was
	 * typed; nothing was written", and a surviving `in_flight` record would make
	 * `/v1/answer/status` answer "still being typed" for that same requestId
	 * forever (nothing advances a record whose lock was never taken), while a
	 * replay would collect `409 lease_held`. The store cannot pick one ordering,
	 * so the caller that needs the rollback asks for it.
	 *
	 * Identity, not requestId alone: if a concurrent attempt has already replaced
	 * the record, the newer one is live and dropping it would strand THAT attempt.
	 * Removal from memory is the guarantee — that is what `get` reads. The rewrite
	 * is attempted and a failure is logged, not thrown: the disk copy (if any)
	 * rehydrates as `unconfirmed`, which §11.5 permits, while the caller's own
	 * loud refusal is already on its way out.
	 */
	forget(record: AnswerAttemptRecord): Promise<void>;
	/** Drops records past the retention. Returns how many. */
	prune(nowMs: EpochMs): Promise<number>;
	/**
	 * The instant from which `known: false` is PROVABLY "nothing was sent".
	 *
	 * The bridge guarantees: for every answer attempt it admitted whose attempt
	 * began at or after this instant, a record exists — so `known: false` for a
	 * request the client sent after it means the request never arrived. Before it,
	 * `known: false` means only "no record", and §11.5 requires the client to
	 * render that as `unconfirmed`, never as failed.
	 *
	 * It is `max(this store's open time, nowMs - retention)`: a record older than
	 * the retention has been pruned, and a record from before this mount cannot be
	 * asserted over at all.
	 *
	 * WHY THIS MOUNT, WHEN THE FILE ITSELF SURVIVES RESTARTS. Hydrated records are
	 * still returned — a pre-restart request is answered from the file exactly as
	 * it was written. What cannot be asserted is that a MISSING record proves the
	 * request never arrived, because `writeFileDurable` cannot force a directory
	 * entry on win32 (`syncDirectory` returns immediately there): a hard reset can
	 * discard this file's most recent rename and revert it to an earlier version.
	 * The reverted file carries the same `coverageSinceMs` as the version that was
	 * lost, so it cannot declare its own gap — the missing records would sit inside
	 * a window still claiming to cover them, which is precisely the "it was not
	 * sent" lie. A rollback needs a crash and therefore a restart, so a window that
	 * starts at this mount is exactly the window a rollback can never reach behind.
	 * Making the file's own stamp load-bearing again requires giving it what
	 * `state-anchor.json` has: a rise-only witness in a second file (SEND-WITNESS
	 * in `keys.ts`), so a reverted file is detected rather than believed.
	 */
	recordsSinceMs(nowMs: EpochMs): EpochMs;
}

/**
 * Opens (and hydrates) the durable attempt store.
 *
 * `dir` is the companion root — already created and ACL-restricted to this user
 * by `ensureCompanionDirs` before this is called.
 *
 * TWO DIFFERENT FAILURES, TWO DIFFERENT ANSWERS:
 *
 *  - the file cannot be READ or WRITTEN (EPERM, EIO, a full disk): THROW. The
 *    bridge would be unable to record the answers it types, and the first write
 *    at the bottom of this function proves the path is usable before a single
 *    request can be served.
 *  - the file is present but MALFORMED (truncated by something that is not this
 *    code, hand-edited, written by a second process): it is moved aside, the
 *    fault is logged, and the store starts EMPTY. This is not tolerance of bad
 *    state — the bad file is preserved for diagnosis and nothing from it is
 *    believed — and it cannot re-open the failure this store exists to close:
 *    the published coverage window starts at this mount either way, so every
 *    request older than this moment reads back as `unconfirmed`, never as "it
 *    was not sent". Throwing instead would turn a scratch file into a total
 *    outage of the phone's only channel, which is the same trade
 *    `device-store`'s pending-destroy list already refuses to make.
 */
export async function createAttemptStore(options: {
	dir: string;
	/** Structured diagnostics. Never carries question or answer text. */
	log: (event: Record<string, unknown>) => void;
	retentionMs?: DurationMs;
	nowMs?: EpochMs;
}): Promise<AttemptStore> {
	const retentionMs = options.retentionMs ?? ANSWER_ATTEMPT_RETENTION_MS;
	const path = join(options.dir, ATTEMPT_STORE_FILENAME);

input.prompt:
Implement a rise-only durable witness for the companion bridge's answer-attempt store, so a CONFIRMED answer's coverage survives a bridge restart.

Repos (use full paths, Windows):
- Fork: `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64`
- Companion (protocol doc): `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion`

## The gap you are closing

Read `packages/host-service/src/companion/answer.ts` lines 1255-1620. The attempt store is durable (`tmp -> fsync -> rename` per put, hydrated at start), but `recordsSinceMs()` publishes a coverage window that starts at THIS MOUNT rather than at the file's own `coverageSinceMs`. The code explains why in the long comment at `recordsSinceMs` (~line 1393-1420) and at `coverageSinceMs` in `attemptFileSchema` (~line 1320-1331): `writeFileDurable` cannot force a directory entry on win32 (`syncDirectory` returns immediately there), so a hard reset can discard the file's most recent rename and revert it to an earlier version. The reverted file carries the SAME `coverageSinceMs` as the version that was lost, so it cannot declare its own gap — missing records would sit inside a window still claiming to cover them, which is the "it was not sent" lie the store exists to remove.

Consequence today: after a restart, a request whose answer actually landed reads back as `unconfirmed` instead of `confirmed`. Honest, but weaker than PROTOCOL §11.5 promises.

Both source comments name the fix explicitly: give the attempts file what `state-anchor.json` already has — a rise-only witness in a second file, so a reverted file is DETECTED rather than believed.

## The pattern to reuse — do not invent a new one

`packages/host-service/src/companion/keys.ts` already implements exactly this (grep `SEND-WITNESS`, `send-witness.json`, `raiseWitness`, `readSendWitness`, `writeSendWitness`, roughly lines 115-130, 240-250, 360-560, 760-800). Read it properly before writing anything. Copy its structure, its generation binding, and its write ORDERING.

Two properties of that pattern are load-bearing and you must preserve both:

1. **Witness is written BEFORE the main file, always.** keys.ts documents (~line 440-460 and ~line 760-770) that what makes the witness's rename durable is the MAIN file's subsequent content fsync — the rename record sits in the same directory metadata log that the fsync flushes. A witness-only write path is therefore NOT durable. Every witness raise must be followed by the attempts-file durable write, in the same directory. Never add a witness-only write path.
2. **Generation binding.** The witness carries the install `generation` (16 random bytes base64url, minted once per install, owned by the state anchor in keys.ts). A witness whose generation does not match means the anchor was deleted/replaced while the witness survived, and nothing can prove freshness.

## CRITICAL divergence from keys.ts — do not copy its fatality

keys.ts throws `StateRollbackError` and REFUSES TO START on a witness mismatch, because a rolled-back send-nonce counter repeats a nonce and that destroys AES-GCM outright. **The attempt store must NOT do this.** A reverted attempts file only costs idempotency/status records. The correct response is to DEGRADE the published coverage window to this mount (exactly today's behaviour) and log loudly — never to refuse to start. `createAttemptStore`'s own header already states the equivalent trade for a malformed file ("throwing instead would turn a scratch file into a total outage of the phone's only channel"). Same reasoning applies here. If you make a benign file revert fatal, you have broken the bridge.

## What to build

- A witness file alongside `answer-attempts.json` in the same companion root directory, recording the install `generation` plus a rise-only monotonic mark that advances on every `put`. Choose the mark deliberately and justify it in a comment — a per-put sequence counter is the obvious candidate; whatever you choose must make "this file is behind what was witnessed" decidable.
- On hydrate: compare witness to file. Match (or no witness yet, first run after upgrade) => the file is current, so `recordsSinceMs` may now start from the file's own `coverageSinceMs` (still floored by the retention: `max(coverageSinceMs, nowMs - retentionMs)`). Witness AHEAD of the file => rollback detected: degrade to mount time, log loudly. Generation mismatch => degrade to mount time, log loudly. Never throw for any of these.
- `createAttemptStore` currently takes `{dir, log, retentionMs?, nowMs?}` and has no access to the anchor's generation. Thread the generation in from the call site (find it — it is in `packages/host-service/src/companion/index.ts`, where keys/anchor are already available). Validate it at that boundary; a missing/malformed generation must degrade to mount-time coverage, not crash. Follow the project rule: validate at API boundaries, fail fast and loud.
- Update the two long comments in answer.ts that currently describe this as future work so they describe what the code now does. They are load-bearing documentation, not decoration — a stale comment here is a correctness hazard for the next reader.
- Update `PROTOCOL.md` §11.5 in the companion repo to describe the new coverage guarantee and the degraded case honestly.

## Hard constraints — violating any of these fails the task

- Never collapse `pending` / `confirmed` / `failed` / `unconfirmed` / `in_flight` into "sent". Honest failure states are the point of this subsystem.
- Do not weaken the six-guard answer transaction under one lock, the answer-wide lease, the byte-contract refusals in `keystrokes.ts`, or the existing anti-rollback anchor/witness in keys.ts.
- Do not touch: `FEATURES.md`, `scripts/ci-repair.sh`, any file under `scripts/`, build files, `package.json`, `bun.lock`, `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. (I handle the FEATURES.md marker myself — CRLF trap.)
- Keep `put` durable. This change is about making coverage PROVABLE, not about relaxing fsync discipline.
- Match the surrounding comment density and voice. This file explains WHY at length; a bare implementation with no rationale is not acceptable here.

Read `packages/host-service/src/companion/answer.ts` lines 1255-1620. The attempt store is durable (`tmp -> fsync -> rename` per put, hydrated at start), but `recordsSinceMs()` publishes a coverage window that starts at THIS MOUNT rather than at the file's own `coverageSinceMs`. The code explains why in the long comment at `recordsSinceMs` (~line 1393-1420) and at `coverageSinceMs` in `attemptFileSchema` (~line 1320-1331): `writeFileDurable` cannot force a directory entry on win32 (`syncDirectory` returns immediately there), so a hard reset can discard the file's most recent rename and revert it to an earlier version. The reverted file carries the SAME `coverageSinceMs` as the version that was lost, so it cannot declare its own gap — missing records would sit inside a window still claiming to cover them, which is the "it was not sent" lie the store exists to remove.

Consequence today: after a restart, a request whose answer actually landed reads back as `unconfirmed` instead of `confirmed`. Honest, but weaker than PROTOCOL §11.5 promises.

Both source comments name the fix explicitly: give the attempts file what `state-anchor.json` already has — a rise-only witness in a second file, so a reverted file is DETECTED rather than believed.

`packages/host-service/src/companion/keys.ts` already implements exactly this (grep `SEND-WITNESS`, `send-witness.json`, `raiseWitness`, `readSendWitness`, `writeSendWitness`, roughly lines 115-130, 240-250, 360-560, 760-800). 1. **Witness is written BEFORE the main file, always.** keys.ts documents (~line 440-460 and ~line 760-770) that what makes the witness's rename durable is the MAIN file's subsequent content fsync — the rename record sits in the same directory metadata log that the fsync flushes. A witness-only write path is therefore NOT durable. Every witness raise must be followed by the attempts-file durable write, in the same directory. Never add a witness-only write path.

input.prompt:
Adversarial correctness review of one focused change to a Windows desktop "companion bridge" (lets a phone/watch answer a blocked AI agent's question by injecting keystrokes into a terminal).

Diffs to review (already captured, read these files):
- `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\tmp\witness-review.diff` (695 lines — answer.ts, index.ts, types.ts)
- `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\tmp\witness-protocol.diff` (90 lines — PROTOCOL.md §11.5)

Read the surrounding code for context, not just the diff: `packages/host-service/src/companion/answer.ts` (attempt store ~1255-2000, `handleAnswerStatus` ~2850), and the pattern it copies in `packages/host-service/src/companion/keys.ts` (grep `SEND-WITNESS`, `raiseWitness`).

## What the change is supposed to do

`answer-attempts.json` is a durable 24h idempotency/status store (`tmp -> fsync -> rename` per put). On win32 `writeFileDurable` cannot force a directory entry, so a hard reset can revert the file to an earlier version while its `coverageSinceMs` stamp still claims to cover the records that were lost. Previously `recordsSinceMs()` defensively published a coverage window starting at the CURRENT MOUNT, so `known: false` for a pre-restart request degraded to "unconfirmed" rather than the actionable "it was not sent".

The change adds `answer-attempts-witness.json`: a generation-bound, rise-only rewrite counter (`seq`) raised BEFORE each attempts-file write in the same directory, so a reverted file is detected instead of believed. When it verifies, coverage may start from the file's own stamp (floored by retention). When it cannot, coverage degrades to the mount.

## The invariants that matter — attack these

1. **A degrade must NEVER throw or refuse to start.** keys.ts is fatal on witness mismatch (a repeated nonce destroys AES-GCM); this store must only narrow its coverage window. Look for any path — malformed witness, missing witness, unreadable, generation mismatch, absent generation, unlink failure, disk full — that can propagate instead of degrading. A crash here bricks the phone's only channel.
2. **Coverage must never over-claim.** `recordsSinceMs` is an ASSERTION that for every admitted attempt at/after that instant a record exists. Find any ordering, concurrency, or crash interleaving where the witness verifies but records are genuinely missing — that is the "it was not sent" lie about an answer that actually landed, the worst outcome in this system.
3. **Rise-only really is rise-only.** Can `seq` be lowered, reused, or reset? Two `persist()` calls racing? A `forget()`/`prune()` rewrite? Check the witness is raised before the attempts write on EVERY path that writes the file, and that a witness-only write path was not introduced (the design note says the attempts file's own content fsync is what publishes the witness's rename, so an unpaired witness write is not durable).
4. **Status honesty.** `pending`/`confirmed`/`failed`/`unconfirmed`/`in_flight`/`unknown` must never collapse into "sent". Verify `handleAnswerStatus` still returns the recorded status unconditionally when a record exists, and that the new proof fields (`serverTimeMs`, `recordsSinceMs`, `bridgeStartedMs`) cannot make a client conclude "not sent" for a request that was.
5. **Two deliberate decisions to scrutinise.** (a) A degrade ADVANCES the file's own `coverageSinceMs` to the mount instant before rewriting, so the gap is recorded once. Is that sound, or does it destroy information / mislead a later mount? (b) A missing or non-canonical generation `unlink`s the witness, so an unwitnessed mount cannot leave a stale witness that the next mount reads as merely "behind" (the harmless direction) and therefore believes. Is the unlink correct, and is it safe if it fails?
6. **Comment accuracy.** This codebase treats its long comments as load-bearing documentation. The change rewrote several that had become false. Verify every rewritten comment now matches the code — a confidently wrong comment here is a correctness hazard.

## Ground rules

- Report only defects you can substantiate with a concrete failure scenario: inputs/state -> wrong outcome. No style notes, no speculation.
- Distinguish CONFIRMED (you traced it) from PLAUSIBLE (needs a run to settle).
- Rank most severe first. If you find nothing real, say so plainly — do not manufacture findings.
- You may run things. A proof harness exists at `tmp/attempt-witness-proof.ts` (24 checks, currently passing): `cd` to the fork root and `bun ./tmp/attempt-witness-proof.ts`. Note `bun run tmp/x.ts` misresolves to package scripts — use `bun ./tmp/x.ts`. Piping through `tail`/`grep` masks exit codes (use `${PIPESTATUS[0]}`).
- Known and already explained, do not report: `tmp/attempt-store-proof2.ts` crashes because it omits the required `log` option (invalid caller); `tmp/attempt-store-proof.ts` and `tmp/verify-attempt-store-fixes.ts` each have one failing check that asserts the OLD mount-start behaviour this change deliberately replaced. Biome reports CRLF errors on these files identically on unmodified HEAD blobs (pre-existing repo-wide EOL).

Do not edit any source file — review only. Report findings.

76:| Companion question capture | the `PreToolUse` AskUserQuestion hook payload already carries everything needed to DISCOVER and render a blocking question — `tool_name`, `tool_use_id`, `transcript_path`, `session_id`, `cwd`, `tool_input.questions[]` (`question`/`header`/`multiSelect`/`options[]`) plus `agent_id`/`agent_type` when a subagent asked — so the capture path forwards it to the bridge's question store instead of parsing transcripts (measured: 300 blocking questions over 7 days, 97.7% answerable, median 1 412 chars, 59% multi-question, ~10% multiSelect). Question text is captured VERBATIM and never truncated: a question longer than the terminal window was never retained in scrollback, so the screen can verify a picker but can never be its source | `(COMPANION-CAPTURE)` |
77:| Companion pairing surface (desktop) | the entry point the phone's own instructions name — "open Superset and choose 'Pair a device'" — without which the companion feature cannot be bootstrapped at all: `openPairing` is reachable only from the desktop's authenticated tRPC surface, so nothing else can ever open the one 120 s LAN window. A row in Experimental settings reads `companion.status` and derives its own availability (off / enabled-but-failed-to-start / running are three different messages, because they need three different actions from the user) rather than offering a button that can only fail; it opens a fork-only dialog that renders the returned URI as a QR and counts the window down. The pairing code lives in the URL FRAGMENT, so the dialog is the only thing that ever holds it: it is never logged, never persisted, never an attribute, never selectable text (a screenshot of a QR expires in 120 s; a screenshot of the string does not), and the flow component is unmounted on close so the value dies with the dialog. Dismissing takes the 0.0.0.0:47611 listener down instead of leaving it up for the rest of the window, and every window operation is serialised because the bridge allows exactly one process-wide (an unserialised close could land after a later open and silently kill the new window). States are honest and bounded — opening / open-with-time-remaining / expired / failed-with-the-server's-reason, never an unbounded spinner. It does NOT claim "paired": the bridge exposes no completion signal to the desktop, so the expiry copy points at the phone, which does know. QR is drawn by a dependency-free byte-mode encoder (level M, versions 1-40, full mask selection) — a QR library would move `package.json`/`bun.lock` under the `(LOCK-REGEN)` gate — always dark-on-white regardless of theme, since an inverted symbol is unreadable to some decoders | `(COMPANION-PAIRING-UI)`, `(COMPANION-PAIRING-ENTRY)`, `(COMPANION-PAIRING-SEARCH)` |
78:| Companion bridge (phone/watch) | fork-only host-service subsystem (`packages/host-service/src/companion/`) that lets a paired Android phone/watch read agent status and answer a blocked AskUserQuestion. Loopback listener on a fixed port behind a Cloudflare tunnel + Access service token, with the bridge validating the Access JWT itself and failing closed; every body is an end-to-end AES-256-GCM sealed envelope keyed on a per-device key that is DERIVED at pairing and never transmitted, with method/path/status/nonce bound into the AAD and a disk-persisted replay cache that outlives the freshness window. The client sends semantic intent only — questionId, fingerprint, option indices — so no wire field can express "send these bytes to that terminal"; the bridge owns the picker byte contract, evaluates its six guards and injects inside ONE critical section holding the per-terminal lock in the same process as the pty writer, under an answer-wide lease (per-keystroke locking interleaves two multi-select answers into a third one neither device chose). First-answer-wins, zero write retries, read-the-outcome instead. Push is data-only opaque ids with runtime assertions that make text leakage throw, delayed 3 min so only genuinely-unattended questions buzz. Wire contract: `superset-companion/PROTOCOL.md` | `(COMPANION-BRIDGE)` |

by exactly the number of lines it added.

  - the fenced ```markers block (what scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs parses)
  - the Companion bridge table row's token cell + description (documentation)
"""

import sys

P = r'C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\FEATURES.md'
TOKEN = '(ATTEMPT-WITNESS)'
ROOT = 'packages/host-service/src/companion/answer.ts'

raw = open(P, 'rb').read()
text = raw.decode('utf-8')
cr_before = text.count('\r')

if TOKEN in text:
    print('already registered; no change')
    sys.exit(0)

# --- edit 1: markers block -------------------------------------------------
# Insert after the last companion marker so related tokens stay together.
anchor = '(COMPANION-PANIC-UI)'
idx = text.rindex(anchor)
end = text.index('\n', idx) + 1          # end of that row, including its \n
text = text[:end] + ('%s\t%s\r\n' % (TOKEN, ROOT)) + text[end:]

# --- edit 2: the Companion bridge table row --------------------------------
old_cell = 'Wire contract: `superset-companion/PROTOCOL.md` | `(COMPANION-BRIDGE)` |'
if text.count(old_cell) != 1:
    print('ABORT: table anchor found %d times, expected 1' % text.count(old_cell))
    sys.exit(1)
new_cell = (
    'Wire contract: `superset-companion/PROTOCOL.md`. The 24 h answer-attempt '
    'store is durable and carries a generation-bound rise-only witness beside '
    'it, so a win32 rollback of its own file (the platform cannot force a '
    'directory entry, and a reverted file still claims to cover the records it '
    'lost) is DETECTED rather than believed: coverage narrows to the current '
    'mount and a pre-restart request with no record reports `unconfirmed`, '
    'never the false terminal "it was not sent". A witness fault only ever '
    'narrows that window \u2014 it can never refuse to start, unlike the send-nonce '
    'anchor it borrows the pattern from, where a rollback would repeat a nonce '
    '| `(COMPANION-BRIDGE)`, `(ATTEMPT-WITNESS)` |'
)
text = text.replace(old_cell, new_cell)

open(P, 'wb').write(text.encode('utf-8'))

# --- verify ----------------------------------------------------------------
check = open(P, 'rb').read().decode('utf-8')
rows = [l for l in check.split('\r\n') if l.startswith(TOKEN)]
fences = check.count('```markers')
print('marker row      :', rows)
print('tabs in row     :', rows[0].count('\t') if rows else 'MISSING')
print('markers fences  :', fences, '(expect 1)')
print('CR delta        :', check.count('\r') - cr_before, '(expect 1 = one added line)')
print('table row tokens:', '(ATTEMPT-WITNESS)' in check.split('\r\n')[77])

content.content:
**The coverage reaches back across restarts.** The attempt store is a file, written
`tmp -> fsync -> rename` on every record and hydrated at start, so the 24-hour
retention is unconditional rather than per-lifetime: an answer that landed before a
desktop restart still reads back `confirmed`. That required a second file, because
durability alone was not enough to *assert* over. On win32 nothing can force a
directory entry, so a hard reset can discard the store's most recent rename and
revert it to an earlier version — and the reverted file carries the same
first-recording stamp as the version that was lost, so it cannot declare its own
gap. Records the rollback removed would then sit inside a window still claiming to
cover them, which is precisely the "it was not sent" lie this endpoint exists to
remove. The bridge therefore keeps a **rise-only witness** beside the store,
written before it on every rewrite and bound to the install, so a reverted store is
*detected* rather than believed.

**And it degrades honestly.** When the witness cannot prove the store is current —
it was rolled back, or the witness is missing, unreadable, or bound to a different
install — `recordsSinceMs` collapses to the instant the current bridge lifetime
opened the store, which is where it always used to start: a rollback needs a crash
and therefore a restart, so a window beginning at this mount is one a rollback can
never reach behind. Records already in the file are still returned in every case;
degrading narrows what a *missing* record proves, never what a present one says.
The bridge does not refuse to start over it — losing the phone's only channel to
protect an idempotency file would be the worse failure — and it logs the
degradation loudly on the desktop.

None of that changes what a client implements: read `recordsSinceMs`, compare ages,
and treat everything outside the window as `unconfirmed`. A client MAY instead gate
on `bridgeStartedMs` alone, and that is always **safe** — but it is no longer
**equivalent**, because `recordsSinceMs` can now be earlier than the current
lifetime. Gating on `bridgeStartedMs` forfeits every pre-restart `confirmed` to
`unconfirmed`, which is the exact loss the durable store and its witness were built
to end.

input.new_string:
**The coverage reaches back across restarts.** The attempt store is a file, written
`tmp -> fsync -> rename` on every record and hydrated at start, so the 24-hour
retention is unconditional rather than per-lifetime.

Be precise about which half of this endpoint that fixes, because the obvious reading
is wrong. A **present** record has always survived a restart on its own: the store is
durable, so `known: true` and the record's own `status` come straight back, and no
witness is involved. What needed more was the **absent** record — `known: false` is
an assertion that nothing was ever sent, and durability alone was not enough to
*assert* over. On win32 nothing can force a directory entry, so a hard reset can
discard the store's most recent rename and revert it to an earlier version — and the
reverted file carries the same first-recording stamp as the version that was lost, so
it cannot declare its own gap. Records the rollback removed would then sit inside a
window still claiming to cover them, which is precisely the "it was not sent" lie
this endpoint exists to remove. The bridge therefore keeps a **rise-only witness**
beside the store, written before it on every rewrite and bound to the install, so a
reverted store is *detected* rather than believed.

**And it degrades honestly.** When the witness cannot prove the store is current —
it was rolled back, or the witness is missing, unreadable, or bound to a different
install, or the store predates the witness and so was never witnessable at all —
`recordsSinceMs` collapses to the instant the current bridge lifetime opened the
store, which is where it always used to start: a rollback needs a crash and
therefore a restart, so a window beginning at this mount is one a rollback can never
reach behind. Records already in the file are still returned in every case;
degrading narrows what a *missing* record proves, never what a present one says.
The bridge does not refuse to start over it — losing the phone's only channel to
protect an idempotency file would be the worse failure — and it logs the
degradation loudly on the desktop.

None of that changes what a client implements: read `recordsSinceMs`, compare ages,
and treat everything outside the window as `unconfirmed`. A client MAY instead gate
on `bridgeStartedMs` alone, and that is always **safe** — but it is no longer
**equivalent**, because `recordsSinceMs` can now be earlier than the current
lifetime. What gating on `bridgeStartedMs` forfeits is not any `confirmed` status —
those are returned regardless — but the ability to resolve a **missing** record from
before the restart. Such a request stays `unconfirmed` ("I cannot tell you") instead
of resolving to the actionable terminal "it never arrived", which is the loss the
durable store and its witness were built to end.

=== types.ts: does it repeat the confirmed-survives-because-of-witness claim? ===
	 */
	serverTimeMs: EpochMs;
	/**
	 * The instant from which `known: false` PROVES the request never arrived.
	 *
	 * THE BRIDGE'S GUARANTEE. For every answer attempt this bridge admitted whose
	 * attempt began at or after `recordsSinceMs`, a record exists — the record is
	 * written durably before the terminal lock is taken, so no keystroke can reach
	 * a terminal without one. The value is `max(the store's PROVEN coverage start,
	 * serverTimeMs − 24 h retention)`, so it also moves forward as old records are
	 * pruned.
	 *
	 * IT REACHES BACK PAST THE CURRENT LIFETIME WHENEVER THE STORE CAN PROVE ITS
	 * OWN FILE IS CURRENT. The store survives a restart and is read back, so a
	 * request from before the restart is answered from the hydrated file exactly as
	 * it was written — and the coverage window now covers it too, so an answer that
	 * landed before a restart still reads as `confirmed` instead of decaying to
	 * `unconfirmed`. What that required is a second file: `writeFileDurable` cannot
	 * force a directory entry on win32 (see `syncDirectory`), so a hard reset can
	 * discard the store's most recent rename and revert the file to an earlier
	 * version — and the reverted file carries the same first-recording stamp as the
	 * version that was lost, so it cannot declare its own gap. The missing records
	 * would sit INSIDE a window still claiming to cover them, which is the "it was
	 * not sent" lie this field exists to remove. `(ATTEMPT-WITNESS)` in `answer.ts`
	 * is the rise-only witness that makes that revert DETECTABLE rather than
	 * believed, which is the only reason the file's own stamp may be published.
	 *
	 * WHEN THE WITNESS CANNOT PROVE IT — the file was rolled back, the witness is
	 * missing, unreadable, or bound to another install — this value DEGRADES to the
	 * instant the current lifetime opened the store, which is exactly what it always
	 * used to be: a rollback needs a crash and therefore a restart, so a window
	 * starting at this mount is one a rollback can never reach behind. Records
	 * already in the file are still returned in every case; degrading narrows what a
	 * MISSING record proves, never what a present one says. The client's rule below
	 * is unchanged either way — it reads this field and does not need to know which

content.text:
Agents stopped. Fable's review came back with one real defect and I fixed it.

**Finding: a `seq: 0` legacy file was believed with no witness to vouch for it.** The code degraded a missing witness only when `seq > 0`, reasoning that a file written by a pre-witness build is *legitimately* unwitnessed. It is — and it's also exactly as unverifiable as a deleted one. The old build can lose a rename the same way, reverting the file while its coverage stamp stays put, and the first mount of the new build would publish that stamp as proven. That reopens the precise "it was not sent" lie about an answer that landed — the worst outcome in this system — for the one file the witness cannot vouch for.

I replaced the two-facts rule with one: degrade whenever the stamp claims reach-back that no witness backs, regardless of what wrote it. A fresh install claims nothing, so it degrades nothing and stays silent. Cost is one mount at upgrade — i.e. the behaviour of every build before this change.

Fable also traced and cleared everything else: never-throws-on-degrade, the crash interleavings, rise-only, status honesty, and both beyond-spec decisions. Its verdict on the stamp-advance was that it's not just sound but load-bearing — it's what makes witness *replacement* safe.

Two documentation corrections that matter more than they sound: `PROTOCOL.md` §11.5 and the `types.ts` field docs both still asserted my false premise — that the witness is what keeps `confirmed` across a restart, and that gating on `bridgeStartedMs` forfeits pre-restart `confirmed`. Both wrong, both client-facing. A client author following them would have built the wrong thing.

| proofs | 28/28 + 4 harnesses, all exit 0 |
| REFERR | running |

One gap I won't paper over: **the boot regression can't run.** `packages/host-service/node_modules/better-sqlite3` has vanished since the 157ms boot, and Bun 1.3.14's resolver plugin can't intercept a bare specifier that fails resolution, so the stub route is dead. The witness wiring *is* proven end-to-end against the real `openStateAnchor` and its real minted generation — no degrade on a clean mount, so the feature isn't a silent no-op — but the listener, hostile-input rejection and timing are unverified since before the rebase.

cd "C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64" && git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(host-service): witness the answer-attempt store against win32 rollback (ATTEMPT-WITNESS)

The attempt store is durable, but durability alone could not be ASSERTED over.
win32 cannot force a directory entry, so a hard reset can discard the store's
most recent rename and revert it to an earlier version — and the reverted file
carries the same coverageSinceMs as the version that was lost, so it cannot
declare its own gap. Records the rollback removed then sit inside a window
still claiming to cover them, which is the "it was not sent" lie about an
answer that actually landed. recordsSinceMs therefore published a window that
began at the current mount, and every pre-restart miss degraded to
`unconfirmed` even when the request genuinely never arrived.

Adds answer-attempts-witness.json: a generation-bound, rise-only rewrite
counter raised BEFORE each attempts-file write in the same directory, so the
file's own content fsync publishes the witness's rename (the ordering keys.ts
already relies on for the send-nonce anchor). When it verifies, coverage starts
from the file's own stamp, floored by the retention; a pre-restart request with
no record now resolves to the actionable "it never arrived".

Unlike keys.ts, a witness fault here NEVER refuses to start. A repeated nonce
destroys AES-GCM; a reverted attempts file only costs status records, so every
fault — rollback, generation mismatch, malformed, unreadable, deleted, absent
mark, no generation supplied — narrows the coverage window and logs loudly.
Records already in the file are still served in every case. A degrade also
advances the file's own stamp before rewriting, so the gap is recorded once and
no later clean mount re-asserts over it.

A file with no rewrite mark is NOT trusted, even though a pre-witness build
wrote it legitimately: the old build could lose a rename the same way, and
nothing about such a file can rule that out, so believing it reopened the exact
lie the witness removes. Upgrading costs its pre-restart coverage once.

Also corrects documentation that had it backwards, in PROTOCOL.md §11.5 and the
types.ts field docs: the witness is NOT what keeps a landed answer reading
`confirmed` across a restart — handleAnswerStatus returns the record's own
status whenever the record exists, and it always did. The witness governs the
`known: false` branch only. A client author following the old text would have
built the wrong thing.

createAttemptStore now asserts its `log` option at the boundary: the witness
added a path that logs on an ordinary open, which turned a latent caller
omission into a TypeError thrown from inside the degrade path — the one path
whose whole contract is that it cannot take the bridge down.

Verified: 92/92 feature markers, (REFERR-GATE) clean across all 7 shipped
packages, 0 companion type diagnostics, and 28/28 on a new decision-table proof
plus four existing attempt-store harnesses. Wiring proven end-to-end against
the real openStateAnchor generation — a clean mount logs no degrade, so the
feature is not a silent no-op. The full bridge boot remains unverified since
packages/host-service/node_modules/better-sqlite3 went missing.
EOF

docs(protocol): correct §11.5 coverage semantics and list every degrade case

The reach-back paragraph asserted that a durable store plus its witness is what
lets an answer that landed before a restart read back `confirmed`, and that
gating on bridgeStartedMs alone forfeits every pre-restart `confirmed`. Both are
wrong: a PRESENT record has always survived a restart on its own, because the
store is durable and /v1/answer/status returns the record's own status whenever
it finds one. The witness governs the ABSENT record — the `known: false` claim
that nothing was ever sent — which before it could only be made about the
current bridge lifetime.

MISSING pre-restart record: it stays `unconfirmed` rather than resolving to the
actionable terminal "it never arrived". Stated that way instead, since a client
author following the old text would have concluded the witness was needed to
trust a `confirmed` status.

Also adds the degrade case the list omitted — a store written by a build that
predates the witness, which is unverifiable for the same reason a deleted
witness is and is no longer trusted.
EOF

input.prompt:
Implement the CLIENT half of a status-proof mechanism in an Android/Wear Kotlin project, so the phone and watch can use what the desktop bridge now proves.

Repo: `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion` (Kotlin, Gradle, modules `core/`, `app-phone/`, `app-watch/`). The wire contract is `PROTOCOL.md` — read §11.5 in full first; I updated it minutes ago and it is authoritative.

## Background — what the server now guarantees

`/v1/answer/status` answers "did my answer land?". Two branches:
- a record EXISTS -> `known: true` plus the record's own `status`. This has always survived a desktop restart (the store is durable). Nothing here needs changing.
- NO record -> `known: false`. This is only an assertion that nothing was ever sent WITHIN A COVERAGE WINDOW. Outside it, the honest answer is `unconfirmed` ("I cannot tell you"), never "it was not sent".

The desktop just gained a durable rise-only witness that lets that window reach back past the current bridge lifetime. It publishes three proof fields on every status response: `serverTimeMs`, `recordsSinceMs`, `bridgeStartedMs`.

## The gap you are closing

`core/src/main/java/family/khaira/supersetcompanion/core/protocol/Answer.kt` — `AnswerStatusResponse` (around line 373) models only six fields and omits all three proof fields. And `BridgeCompanionRepository.unknownRequestOutcome` still decides "not sent" by comparing `bridgeStartedMs` for equality. Its own comment says the missing fields "would recover that case exactly… unknown fields are ignored until then (§0)". Find both — grep for `unknownRequestOutcome` and `AnswerStatusResponse`.

Current behaviour is SAFE but lossy: a missing pre-restart record degrades to `Unconfirmed` even when the server can now prove it never arrived.

## What to build

1. Add `serverTimeMs`, `recordsSinceMs`, `bridgeStartedMs` to `AnswerStatusResponse`, following whatever serialization and validation convention that file already uses for epoch-millis fields. Match the surrounding code — do not invent a new style.

2. Switch `unknownRequestOutcome` to the age comparison PROTOCOL §11.5 specifies. The comparison is on AGES, deliberately not on two wall clocks (client and server clocks are allowed to disagree):

```
coverageAgeMs = serverTimeMs - recordsSinceMs
submitAgeMs   = client's own elapsed time since it submitted the answer
provably-not-sent  <=>  coverageAgeMs > submitAgeMs
```

Use a MONOTONIC clock for the client's own elapsed time, not wall-clock — a wall-clock jump or NTP correction must not be able to manufacture a "not sent" verdict. Find how the codebase already tracks elapsed time for a submitted answer; if there is no monotonic submit timestamp available, say so and tell me rather than substituting wall-clock.

3. When the comparison does NOT hold, the outcome stays `Unconfirmed`. Never `Failed`, never anything that reads as "not sent" — §11.4 records a second answer against a picker as unrecoverable, so a false "not sent" sends the user to re-answer a picker that was already answered.

## Hard constraints

- Honest states must not collapse. Whatever the outcome type is (`Confirmed`/`Unconfirmed`/`Failed`/`NotSent` or similar), each must stay distinct and mean exactly what it says.
- Server fields are UNTRUSTED input: validate at the boundary. A missing, negative, non-numeric, or nonsensical proof field (e.g. `recordsSinceMs > serverTimeMs`) must fall back to `Unconfirmed`, not throw and not produce a "not sent".
- Backward compatible: a bridge that does not send the three fields must still work, degrading to today's `bridgeStartedMs` behaviour. §0 says unknown fields are ignored; the reverse — absent fields — must be handled too.
- Do NOT touch: `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, any build file, `local.properties`, or anything under `keystore/`. Do not add dependencies.
- Phone and watch may both consume this. Check both and keep them consistent.

## Verify before reporting

Build it. From `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion`:
```
./gradlew assembleDebug
```
That is the real gate — it must pass. Report the verbatim tail of the output. If tests exist for the repository or the outcome logic, run them; if none exist, write a focused unit test for the age comparison covering: provably-not-sent, inside-coverage-so-unconfirmed, absent proof fields, and a hostile `recordsSinceMs > serverTimeMs`. Say clearly which of those you ran versus only reasoned about.

Notes: Gradle here is configured for a portable JDK/SDK under `~/dev-tools`; if the wrapper cannot find a JDK, report that rather than installing anything. `local.properties` deliberately uses forward slashes — a single backslash is a Java properties escape and mangles the path.

Report: the diff you made, the monotonic-clock decision and why, the validation you added at the boundary, and the verbatim build result. If any part of this is wrong or unsafe, say so plainly instead of implementing it badly. Do not commit.

| | |

| hostile input | 403 before parsing — garbage, 4MB body, empty; unknown path 404 |
| alive after | yes |
| witness in a real boot | `seq=1`, generation `ythK4qdv…` **bound to the anchor**, no degrade |

That last row is the thing that was missing — the wiring is now proven in an actual bridge boot, not just against `openStateAnchor` in isolation. The ACL re-verify also fired live and re-applied owner-only permissions, as designed.

How I got there matters for your expectations: the binding was a **dangling symlink**, not a missing package — which is why `ls -d` succeeded and reading it failed. Rather than attempt a win-arm64 native compile (the thing this fork builds in CI precisely so you don't have to), I placed a documented non-functional stub in both root and `host-service` `node_modules`. Both are gitignored, `bun.lock` is untouched, and any real `bun install` replaces them. The limitation carries over unchanged: **DB-backed paths — agent tree, transcripts — see an empty database.** Those remain unproven locally.

name: reference-companion-boot-harness-sqlite
description: How to actually BOOT the companion bridge locally — better-sqlite3 is a dangling symlink, not a missing package, and the fix is a stub in gitignored node_modules (never a native win-arm64 compile)
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Booting the companion bridge locally (`tmp/boot-bridge.ts` in the fork) needs
`better-sqlite3` to *resolve*. It normally does not, and the failure is misleading:

- `ls -d packages/host-service/node_modules/better-sqlite3` **succeeds** while
  `ls -la` on the same path fails. It is a **dangling symlink** (bun links
  workspace deps), not an absent package. Don't conclude "never installed".
- Bun 1.3.14's `plugin({ setup: b => b.onResolve(...) })` does **not** intercept a
  bare specifier that fails resolution, so `--preload` stub tricks cannot work.
  `tmp/preload-stub.ts` is dead for this purpose.
- The real importer is `drizzle-orm`'s `better-sqlite3/driver.js` inside
  `node_modules/.bun/...`, so resolution walks up to **root** `node_modules`.
  Stubbing only `packages/host-service/node_modules` is not enough — put it in
  BOTH.

Fix that works: a hand-written CommonJS stub package (`package.json` with
`main: index.js`, plus a `Database`/`Statement` class where every query returns
empty) in `node_modules/better-sqlite3` at root **and** in
`packages/host-service/node_modules/`. `node_modules` is gitignored, so
`bun.lock` and the repo stay untouched and any real `bun install` replaces it.

**Never** attempt a native win-arm64 `better-sqlite3` compile locally — building
that closure in CI is the entire point of this fork.

What a stubbed boot does and does not prove:
- PROVES: `start()` completes (~150ms), the listener arms, hostile input is
  refused before parsing, ACL re-verify fires, and the `(ATTEMPT-WITNESS)`
  wiring lands a witness bound to the real anchor generation with no degrade.
- DOES NOT prove: anything DB-backed — agent tree, transcripts — which see an
  empty database. State that rather than implying full coverage.

`/v1/ping` returning **403 access_denied** to a local probe is CORRECT, not a
regression: ping is *unsealed* (no AES-GCM envelope) but still calls
`accessValidator.validate()` with no no-config bypass, and only Cloudflare's edge
can mint the `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion` it needs. A local 200 on ping is
unreachable by design.

input.prompt:
Thorough correctness review of the SERVER half of an anti-rollback mechanism. Report defects only — no style notes.

Commit: `d28f53506` in `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64`. See it with `git show d28f53506` (536 insertions across answer.ts, index.ts, types.ts, FEATURES.md). Read the surrounding code, not only the diff.

## What it does

`packages/host-service/src/companion/answer.ts` holds a durable 24h store of answer attempts (`answer-attempts.json`, `tmp -> fsync -> rename` per put). It answers "did my answer land?" for a phone/watch that answered a blocked AI agent's question by having the desktop inject keystrokes into a terminal.

Two branches: a record EXISTS -> `known: true` + its status. NO record -> `known: false`, which is an ASSERTION that nothing was ever sent, valid only inside a published coverage window (`recordsSinceMs`).

On win32 `writeFileDurable` cannot force a directory entry, so a hard reset can discard the file's most recent rename and revert it to an earlier version whose `coverageSinceMs` still claims to cover the lost records. The change adds `answer-attempts-witness.json`: a generation-bound rise-only rewrite counter (`seq`), raised BEFORE each attempts-file write in the same directory so the attempts file's own content fsync publishes the witness's rename. Verified -> coverage may start at the file's own stamp; unverified -> degrades to the current mount.

## Attack these specifically

1. **Over-claim.** Any interleaving — concurrent puts, crash between writes, prune, forget, quarantine, retention floor — where the witness VERIFIES but records are genuinely missing. That produces a false "it was not sent" for an answer that landed, which §11.4 calls unrecoverable because the user re-answers a picker. This is the worst outcome in the system; weight it accordingly.
2. **Any path that can throw instead of degrading.** A witness fault must only narrow the window, never take the bridge down (unlike `keys.ts`, where a rolled-back send-nonce is correctly fatal because a repeated nonce destroys AES-GCM). Consider ENOSPC, EPERM, EACCES, EBUSY, a directory where a file is expected, a read that succeeds but returns garbage, unlink failure, and the boundary assert I added for the `log` option.
3. **Rise-only.** Can `seq` be lowered, reset, or reused? Look hard at `raiseWitness`, the `persist()` promise-tail serialisation, the `Math.max` on load, and whether a witness-only write path exists anywhere (the durability argument depends on the witness write always being followed by the attempts-file write in the same directory).

Thorough correctness review of the CLIENT half of a status-proof mechanism in an Android/Wear Kotlin app. Report defects only — no style notes.

Commit: `f25e438` in `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion`. See it with `git show f25e438` (478 insertions: `core/.../protocol/Answer.kt`, `app-phone/.../data/BridgeCompanionRepository.kt`, `app-phone/.../data/CompanionRepository.kt`, new `core/src/test/.../AnswerStatusCoverageTest.kt`). Read the surrounding code, not only the diff. `PROTOCOL.md` §11.5 is the authoritative contract — read it.

## Context

The app lets the user answer a blocked AI agent's question from a phone or watch; a desktop bridge injects the keystrokes. `/v1/answer/status` answers "did my answer land?".

- record EXISTS -> `known: true` + the record's own status. Always survived a desktop restart (the store is durable). Untouched by this change.
- NO record -> `known: false`, which asserts nothing was ever sent, but ONLY inside a coverage window the server publishes.

The server just gained a durable witness letting that window reach back past the current bridge lifetime, and publishes `serverTimeMs`, `recordsSinceMs`, `bridgeStartedMs`. This commit consumes them via an age comparison:

```
coverageAgeMs = serverTimeMs - recordsSinceMs
submitAgeMs   = client's elapsed time since it submitted
provably-not-sent  <=>  coverageAgeMs > submitAgeMs
```

Ages, not wall clocks, because the two clocks may disagree. The client side uses `SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()` (monotonic from boot).

## Attack these specifically

1. **False "not sent".** Any input or state where `unknownRequestOutcome` returns `Failed`/"it was not sent" for an answer that actually landed. This is the worst outcome: §11.4 records re-answering a picker as unrecoverable, so this sends the user to corrupt their own agent session. Consider hostile/absent/edge server values, `recordsSinceMs > serverTimeMs`, negatives, zero, `Long.MAX_VALUE`, overflow in the subtraction, and a bridge that lies.
2. **The monotonic clock.** `elapsedRealtime()` counts from boot and does NOT survive a device reboot. Trace what happens to `writeLifetimes[requestId]` across: app process death, device reboot, the watch relaying a requestId this phone never sent, and a submit recorded before a reboot compared against an elapsed value after one. Can any of those manufacture a too-SMALL `submitAgeMs` (which is the direction that produces a false "not sent")?
3. **Boundary validation.** These fields cross a trust boundary from a server the client should not blindly believe. Verify absent, malformed, and nonsensical values fall back to `Unconfirmed` and cannot throw. Check how the deserializer handles missing fields versus explicit nulls.
4. **Backward compatibility.** A bridge that sends none of the three fields must still work, degrading to the old `bridgeStartedMs` lifetime-equality behaviour. Verify, including the case where SOME but not all three arrive.
5. **State honesty.** `Confirmed`/`Unconfirmed`/`Failed` (and any other outcome) must stay distinct and mean exactly what they say. Nothing may collapse into "sent". Check the UI consumers too — a state rendered as terminal when it is not is the same defect one layer up.
6. **The retention gate.** A submit older than the bridge's 24h retention resolves to `Unconfirmed` ("pruned, not never-sent"), and that gate is claimed to run BEFORE either proof so a bridge claiming a window wider than its own retention cannot widen the verdict. Verify that ordering actually holds and that the client's retention constant matches the server's.
7. **Watch parity.** Check whether `app-watch` has its own copy of this decision or shares the phone's. If it has its own, verify consistency; divergence here means the two surfaces give contradictory answers about the same request.

```
cd "C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/superset-companion"
export JAVA_HOME="C:/Users/khair/dev-tools/jdk-21"; export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
./gradlew assembleDebug --console=plain          # currently BUILD SUCCESSFUL
./gradlew :core:testDebugUnitTest --console=plain --tests '*AnswerStatusCoverageTest'   # 16/16
```

Do NOT run a bare `:core:testDebugUnitTest` and report it as a failure: `CrossRuntimeDifferentialVectors20260729Test` deliberately throws unless `SC_KOTLIN_VECTOR_FILE` is set, and it runs via its own harness (`tmp/differential_vectors/run-differential.ps1` in the sibling fork repo, currently 154/154 PASS). That is by design, not a defect.

Extend `AnswerStatusCoverageTest` with new cases if that is how you substantiate a finding — that file is fair game. Do NOT touch `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, build files, `local.properties`, or anything under `keystore/`. Do not add dependencies. Do not commit.

For each finding: file:line, one-line claim, concrete failure scenario (inputs/state -> wrong outcome), CONFIRMED vs PLAUSIBLE. Most severe first. If you find nothing real, say so plainly rather than manufacturing findings.

input.prompt:
Review the CONTRACT between a TypeScript server and a Kotlin client for disagreement. Two teams' worth of code changed in the same hour, in two repos, and nobody has checked that the halves actually agree. That is your only job. Report defects only.

Commits:
- Server: `d28f53506` in `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64` (`git show d28f53506`)
- Client + spec: `f25e438` and `1d407d8` in `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion` (`git show f25e438`, `git show 1d407d8`)

Authoritative spec: `PROTOCOL.md` §11.5 in the companion repo.

## What the feature is

`/v1/answer/status` answers "did the answer I sent from my watch actually land?" A record's presence gives `known: true` + its status. Absence gives `known: false`, which asserts nothing was ever sent — but only inside a coverage window the server publishes as three fields: `serverTimeMs`, `recordsSinceMs`, `bridgeStartedMs`. The client turns those into a verdict via an age comparison:

```
coverageAgeMs = serverTimeMs - recordsSinceMs
submitAgeMs   = client's own elapsed time since it submitted
provably-not-sent  <=>  coverageAgeMs > submitAgeMs
```

A false "not sent" makes the user re-answer a picker, which §11.4 records as unrecoverable. A false "confirmed" makes them trust an answer that never landed. Both halves must agree exactly on when each is claimed.

## Check for disagreement, in this order

1. **Field-level.** Names, JSON casing, types, units (ms vs s), nullability, and whether the server can emit a shape the client's deserializer rejects or silently coerces. Find where the server builds the response (`handleAnswerStatus` in `packages/host-service/src/companion/answer.ts`, types in `types.ts`) and where the client models it (`core/.../protocol/Answer.kt`).
2. **Semantic.** Both sides now describe the same guarantee in prose. Do they mean the same thing? Specifically: the server DEGRADES `recordsSinceMs` to the current mount when its witness cannot prove the store is current — does the client's logic stay correct under a degraded value, and does the client assume anything the server does not promise? Is the strictness of the comparison the same on both sides (`>` vs `>=`)?
3. **Constants.** The 24h retention exists on both sides. Verify they match and that neither can drift silently. Flag any other duplicated constant governing this endpoint.
4. **The spec against both implementations.** §11.5 was rewritten in `1d407d8`. Verify it now describes what the server actually does AND what the client actually does. Specifically check the degrade-case list is complete (the server degrades on: rollback detected, witness missing, unreadable, bound to another install, no rewrite mark, and no generation supplied) and that no sentence claims something neither side implements. A prior version of that text asserted the witness is what keeps a landed answer reading `confirmed` across a restart — that was FALSE (a present record always survived, because the store is durable) and was corrected. Look for any surviving trace of that error in either repo, including code comments.
5. **Forward/backward compatibility.** An old client against the new server, and a new client against an old server that sends none of the three fields. Both must be safe. §0 says unknown fields are ignored; verify absent fields are handled too, and that a partial set (one or two of three) cannot produce a wrong verdict.
6. **Anything the spec promises that neither side implements**, or that only one side does.

## Verification available

Server (Git Bash, fork root): `bun ./tmp/attempt-witness-proof.ts` (28 checks), `bun ./tmp/boot-bridge.ts` (real boot; DB paths return empty via a local stub, by design). `node scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs` -> 92.

Client (companion root): `export JAVA_HOME="C:/Users/khair/dev-tools/jdk-21"; export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"; ./gradlew assembleDebug --console=plain` -> SUCCESSFUL; `./gradlew :core:testDebugUnitTest --tests '*AnswerStatusCoverageTest'` -> 16/16.

Cross-runtime byte parity: `tmp/differential_vectors/run-differential.ps1` in the fork (PowerShell) -> 154/154 PASS. Note 4 Kotlin-only properties are the client's X25519 ephemeral keypair, which by construction has no bridge counterpart; that asymmetry is expected.

Do NOT report as findings: `CrossRuntimeDifferentialVectors20260729Test` failing without `SC_KOTLIN_VECTOR_FILE` (deliberate fail-loud, runs via its own harness); Biome CRLF errors in the fork's companion directory (pre-existing, present on untouched files); the 8 `tsc` debt diagnostics outside `src/companion/`.

Traps: `bun ./tmp/x.ts` not `bun run tmp/x.ts`; piping through `tail`/`grep` masks exit codes.

Do not edit source in either repo; you may add throwaway probes under the fork's `tmp/`. Do not commit.

For each finding: which side is wrong (or whether the spec is), file:line on both sides, and a concrete scenario where the disagreement produces a wrong verdict. CONFIRMED vs PLAUSIBLE. Most severe first. If the two halves genuinely agree, say so plainly.

Robustness and input-validation review of a durable-state consistency mechanism. This is a personal single-user desktop utility; I own all of it and I am asking you to find bugs in my own code before I rely on it.

## Repo and commit

`C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64`, commit `d28f53506`.
See it with `git show d28f53506` — 536 insertions across
`packages/host-service/src/companion/answer.ts`, `index.ts`, `types.ts`, and `FEATURES.md`.
Please read the surrounding code, not just the diff.

## What the software does

A desktop app runs AI coding agents in terminals. When an agent blocks on a multiple-choice
question, a paired phone or watch can answer it: the phone sends the chosen option indices, and a
local bridge process types the corresponding keystrokes into that terminal.

The bridge keeps a durable 24-hour record of every answer attempt in `answer-attempts.json`,
written `tmp -> fsync -> rename` on every change. The phone polls an endpoint that reports:

- a record EXISTS  -> `known: true` plus that record's own status (confirmed / failed /
  unconfirmed / in_flight). This has always survived a desktop restart, because the file is
  durable.
- NO record        -> `known: false`. This is an ASSERTION that nothing was ever typed. It is
  only valid inside a published coverage window, the field `recordsSinceMs`.

Getting `known: false` wrong in the unsafe direction makes the phone tell the user "your answer
was never sent" for an answer that actually landed. The user then answers the same question a
second time, which corrupts the agent's session unrecoverably. That is the worst outcome in this
system and the thing I most want you to hunt for.

## The problem this commit addresses

On Windows, `writeFileDurable` cannot force a directory entry to disk (`syncDirectory` is a no-op
on win32). So a hard reset can discard the attempts file's most recent rename and revert the file
to an earlier version. The reverted file carries the SAME first-recording stamp
(`coverageSinceMs`) as the version that was lost, so it cannot declare its own gap: records the
rollback removed would sit inside a window still claiming to cover them.

Before this commit the code defended against that by publishing a window that always started at
the current process mount, which threw away every pre-restart record's usefulness.

This commit adds `answer-attempts-witness.json`: a small second file holding an install
identifier plus a rise-only counter (`seq`) of how many durable rewrites the attempts file has
had. The counter is raised BEFORE each attempts-file write, in the same directory, so the
attempts file's own content fsync publishes the witness's rename. On startup the two are
compared:

- witness level with or behind the file -> the file is the latest version that was ever durable,
  so its own stamp may be published
- witness AHEAD of the file             -> the file's most recent rename was lost; records are
  gone; narrow the window to this mount
- witness missing / unreadable / malformed / bound to a different install / the file carries no
  counter at all / no install id supplied -> cannot be proven; narrow the window to this mount

A narrowed ("degraded") mount also advances the file's own stamp before rewriting it, so the gap
is recorded once and a later clean mount does not re-assert over it.

Critically, a witness fault must NEVER prevent the bridge from starting. A sibling module
(`keys.ts`) does refuse to start on an equivalent mismatch, because there a rolled-back counter
would repeat an AES-GCM nonce and that is catastrophic. Here the only cost is losing status
records, so refusing to start would take away the phone's only channel for no benefit. Please
check that distinction is actually honoured everywhere.

## What I would like from you

1. Any interleaving — concurrent writes, a crash between the two file writes, prune, forget,
   quarantine of a malformed file, the retention floor — where the witness VERIFIES but records
   are genuinely missing. That is the false "never sent" case.
2. Any path where a witness fault propagates as an exception instead of narrowing the window.
   Consider ENOSPC, EPERM, EACCES, EBUSY, a directory where a file is expected, a read that
   succeeds and returns garbage, and a failing `unlink`.
3. Whether the counter is genuinely rise-only: can it be lowered, reset, or reused? Look at the
   raise function, the promise-tail serialisation of writes, the `Math.max` on load, and whether
   any code path writes the witness WITHOUT a following attempts-file write (the durability
   argument depends on that pairing).
4. Whether advancing the file's own stamp on a degrade destroys information a later mount needs.
5. Whether a file with no counter (written by the previous build) is handled safely. It is
   deliberately NOT trusted — I want you to check that is what the code does, that a brand-new
   install with no file at all does not log a phantom fault, and that an upgrading install still
   SERVES the records it loaded.
6. Correctness of the long explanatory comments against the code. This codebase treats them as
   documentation; one previously claimed the witness is what lets a landed answer still read
   "confirmed" after a restart, which was simply false — the durable file always did that on its
   own — and I corrected it. Please flag any remaining comment that does not match the code.

## Running things

Bun is installed. From the repo root, in a bash shell:

    bun ./tmp/attempt-witness-proof.ts      # 28 checks, the full decision table
    bun ./tmp/attempt-store-proof.ts
    bun ./tmp/attempt-store-proof2.ts
    bun ./tmp/verify-attempt-store-fixes.ts
    bun ./tmp/witness-wiring-probe.ts
    bun ./tmp/boot-bridge.ts                # boots the real bridge against a scratch directory

Use `bun ./tmp/x.ts`, not `bun run tmp/x.ts` — the latter misresolves to package scripts.

    node scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs        # expect: All 92 feature markers present
    node scripts/check-dangerous-diagnostics.mjs  # ~2 minutes

Please do not treat these as findings, they are known and accepted:

- `bunx tsc --noEmit` in `packages/host-service` reports 8 diagnostics; all are pre-existing
  type debt OUTSIDE `src/companion/`. What matters is that diagnostics under `src/companion/`
  are zero.
- Biome reports CRLF formatting errors on every file in that directory, including files this
  commit never touched. Repo-wide line-ending state, not this change.
- `boot-bridge.ts` reports empty results for anything database-backed; a local stub stands in for
  a native SQLite binding that only the CI build produces.

Shell traps that have burned me: piping through `tail` or `grep` masks the real exit code (use
`${PIPESTATUS[0]}`), and `grep -c` exits non-zero when it finds zero matches.

You may add throwaway probe scripts under `tmp/`. Please do not modify anything under
`packages/`, `apps/`, `scripts/`, or `FEATURES.md`, and do not commit.

For each finding give me the file and line, a one-sentence statement of the bug, and a concrete
scenario (starting state and inputs -> wrong result). Tell me which ones you actually reproduced
versus reasoned about, and rank them by severity. If the code is correct, please say so directly
rather than listing minor observations — a clean verdict is a useful result.

One defect has already been found and fixed in this commit by an earlier reviewer: files carrying
no counter used to be trusted. Please don't re-report that as open, though do check my fix.
