content.subject: Clamp the coverage window against a forward desktop clock step (H3)
content.description:
From fable-rev-honesty, PLAUSIBLE but the consequence is the unrecoverable one. Distinct from D6 (which is about pruned records and is bounded by the client contract); this one produces the actual user-visible lie.

H3: the "ages not wall clocks" design only cancels PHONE-vs-DESKTOP skew. coverageAgeMs = serverTimeMs - recordsSinceMs is a wall-clock difference taken across time on ONE machine (both from Date.now() on the desktop), so a FORWARD step of the desktop clock between coverage start and the query inflates the claimed window by the step size.

Scenario: hard reset rolls the attempts file back and records are lost -> witness degrades, coverage = mount instant (wall clock). Desktop clock then corrects forward 1h (NTP fixing a slow clock, or a user time change). The user's answer landed 40 min ago, pre-crash, and its record was lost. Client computes submitAgeMs 40min < coverageAgeMs ~1h -> provesNeverSent -> user is told "the desktop never saw this request — it was not sent" for an answer that landed -> re-answers the picker -> §11.4 unrecoverable.

Exposure is confined to the coverage=mount (degraded) cases, because a witness-verified window implies no record loss and those windows are retention-floored. That is what makes it clampable.

Fix options: (a) server-side, when degraded, publish recordsSinceMs such that coverageAgeMs <= monotonic elapsed since mount (anchor on process.hrtime rather than Date.now()); or (b) client-side, cap proof 1 with proof 2's lifetime bracket. (a) is better — it fixes the claim at the source rather than making every client compensate.

Backward steps are already safe: recordsSinceMs > serverTimeMs -> coverageAgeMs null -> Unconfirmed, and that is already tested.

Note the shared root with D6: both are Date.now() being treated as monotonic. A single fix — anchoring published instants to a monotonic source — may close both. Consider that before fixing them separately.

content.subject: Witness durability rests on an undocumented rename-ordering assumption
content.description:
From sol-contract (GPT-5.6 Sol, ultra). This questions the premise the whole mechanism rests on, and the same premise underpins keys.ts SEND-WITNESS.

THE CLAIM (crypto.ts:1046, answer.ts:1410, answer.ts:1942): the witness write is made durable by the ATTEMPTS file's subsequent content fsync, because the witness's rename record sits in the same directory metadata log that the fsync flushes.

SOL'S OBJECTION: Microsoft documents FlushFileBuffers as flushing THE SPECIFIED FILE, and states a volume handle is required to flush all files on a volume. MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH exists as a SEPARATE, explicit move-durability guarantee, and Node exposes no equivalent durable-rename option. So "F's fsync publishes W's rename" is an incidental filesystem ordering assumption, not a documented guarantee.

IF IT IS WRONG: witness W and attempts file F can both roll back to a matching version n-1. The next mount then sees EQUAL counters, logs no degradation, has lost the record, and publishes the old coverage — and the client reports a landed answer as "never sent". That is the exact failure the witness was built to prevent, and it would be invisible.

EVIDENCE STATUS, stated honestly by Sol: it restored both pre-write files and reproduced known:false with zero degradation events and a true client age comparison — i.e. the POSTCONDITION is confirmed harmful. Whether a real NTFS hard reset can actually produce that joint rollback is REASONED, not power-cut reproduced.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THIS COMMIT: keys.ts's SEND-WITNESS relies on the identical assumption for send-nonce anti-rollback, where the consequence is AES-GCM nonce reuse. If the assumption is unsound, that mechanism is weaker than its comments claim too — though it fails closed (refuses to start) rather than lying.

WHAT TO DO — do not silently "fix" this, it needs a decision:
(a) Get authoritative evidence: a documented NTFS/Windows guarantee, or a real crash-consistency test (power-cut / VM reset harness), or
(b) Weaken the comments to state it as a best-effort ordering assumption rather than a proof, and say what is NOT covered, or
(c) Find a construction that does not depend on cross-file rename ordering at all — e.g. put the counter INSIDE the attempts file plus a separate append-only (never renamed) witness log, since append+fsync has no rename to lose. Note the replay cache is already structurally immune for exactly this reason (append+fsync per admit, rename only at compaction where a lost rename reverts to a SUPERSET = conservative).

Option (c) is the only one that removes the doubt rather than documenting it.

content.subject: Sol findings: clock (S1), lifetime aliasing (S2), in_flight polling (S3), boundary validation (S4)
content.description:
From sol-contract (ultra). Items not already tracked in #18-#21.

S1 (CONFIRMED, upgrades H3/D6 from plausible to reproduced) Sol reproduced the clock defect end-to-end with the real store and handler, and its scenario is better than the one I recorded: a landed record is 23 REAL hours old; the desktop clock jumps forward 2h; prune sees 25h and deletes it; the server advertises a 24h coverage age while the phone measures ~23h; 24h > 23h -> "never sent". Measured: record absent, degradation events none, coverageAgeMs 86,400,000, monotonic submit age 60,000, client predicate TRUE. This merges D6 (#20) and H3 (#21) into ONE confirmed defect: wall time treated as monotonic. Fix at the source with a monotonic anchor.

S2 (NEW) bridgeStartedMs is only Date.now() (index.ts:323) but the client treats equality as exact lifetime IDENTITY (BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:88). Repeated wall time can alias two different bridge lifetimes, making the fallback proof unsafe. Fix: mint a per-lifetime random/monotonic id, or combine Date.now() with the install generation + a counter.

S3 (NEW, medium) `in_flight` is never re-polled. The server durably records in_flight before typing (answer.ts:2383) and the repository correctly maps it to Pending (BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:431), but the phone performs exactly one status read, "never in a loop" (ConversationViewModel.kt:383), and the watch converts Pending to unknown (WatchBridge.kt:529). PROTOCOL.md:1721 and :1732 REQUIRE pending display and continued polling. Scenario: the status read lands during the ~15s injection window; the server later records confirmed; the phone stays Pending until the user intervenes and the watch shows Unconfirmed. Either implement bounded polling or change the spec — but they must agree.

S4 (NEW, medium) No cross-field or echoed-id validation at either boundary. The server's untrusted-disk schema validates fields independently (answer.ts:1314) and emits them unchanged (answer.ts:2948), so it will happily serve `confirmed` with `resolvedAtMs: null`. Per NON-NEGOTIABLE RULE 1 the SERVER should reject that shape at its own disk boundary, not just have the client cope (which is F2). Separately the client never checks the echoed requestId (Answer.kt:425, BridgeClient.kt:246), so a future erroneous response for request B could settle A — currently unreachable because response AAD binds the request nonce.

S5 (NEW, low) PROTOCOL §11.5 (PROTOCOL.md:1645) declares the proof fields required and non-null, while the Kotlin serializer coerces missing, null, fractional, quoted, object, boolean and overflow values to null (Answer.kt:385). Missing fields NEED that exception for old-server compatibility, but the spec does not say so — and coercing MALFORMED values contradicts §0's hard-error rule. Decide which rule wins and make both sides state it.

S6 The false "witness preserves confirmed after restart" claim also survives in the harness itself, tmp/attempt-witness-proof.ts:70 — so the fix list for D1 is five sites, not four.

S7 The retention constant can drift silently: no shared vector or cross-repo assertion covers it. Consider adding it to the differential vector set, which already crosses the language boundary.

CONFIRMED CLEAN by Sol, agreeing with earlier passes: all nine JSON keys/casing/status spellings/units align; the server always emits all three proof fields on both branches; strict `>` in spec, server docs, client and tests; negative/reversed/absent/half windows conservatively lose proof; a degraded window is correct while the wall clock stays continuous; known:true responses are unaffected by degradation; all three compatibility directions are safe.

content.subject: CRITICAL: detached prune from a stopped store clobbers the new store and lowers the counter
content.description:
From sol-crash-consistency (GPT-5.6 Sol ultra, EXECUTED with a probe against the real implementation). This is the most severe finding of the entire review: it needs no filesystem assumption, no clock step, and no wiring fault — just a stop/start while an hourly prune is in flight.

MECHANISM (verified by me): index.ts:654-657 fires `interval(HOUR_MS, async () => { await attempts.prune(Date.now()); ... })`. Teardown (index.ts:685-689) only does `clearInterval(timer)` — it NEVER awaits an in-flight callback. So a prune already executing when the bridge stops keeps a live reference to the OLD AttemptStore closure (its records map, its seq, its paths). Serialization and the witness read/write guard are per-INSTANCE only (answer.ts:1892-1967), so the old instance's persist() has no idea a new instance exists.

SEQUENCE (Sol's probe output): old store at F/W=2 begins prune and reads W=2 -> stop/start creates a new store which reaches F/W=3, then records an answer at F/W=4 -> the old prune resumes and writes its stale empty snapshot as W=3, F=3. Measured: before releasing the old prune F=4/W=4 records [old,new]; after F=3/W=3 records []; on reopen no degradation, the new record absent, old coverage retained. The next restart therefore TRUSTS a matching pair while a recorded answer has been destroyed -> false "it was not sent".

THIS BREAKS THE RISE-ONLY CLAIM. I verified rise-only within one instance and reported it as holding; it does not hold across instances. Math.max and the promise tail cannot see another instance's writes.

BROADER CLASS: the same detached-interval pattern covers nonceCache.compact, audit.prune and deviceStore.purgeExpiredRevocations in the same block. Check whether any of those can also clobber a successor's state. The nonce cache is the one to look at hardest, since its rollback consequence is the fatal one.

FIX DIRECTIONS: (a) make teardown await in-flight maintenance, not just clear timers — track the in-flight promise and await it in the unwind entry; (b) give each store instance an ownership token and have persist() refuse if it is no longer the owner (the anchor already has this shape for the send-nonce lifecycle); (c) both. (b) defends even against a leaked reference that outlives teardown.

Also from the same report, comment errors this invalidates: index.ts:699-704 and 723-724 claim teardown prevents old writers overlapping a new bridge — detached maintenance makes that false. And answer.ts:1457 / 1877-1882 claim witness-ahead PROVES an attempts-file version was durably written and then lost; a failure between the witness raise and the primary write produces the identical state with no such version ever existing.

content.subject: Lead: an r+ directory handle may be fsync-able on Windows, which would retire the ordering assumption
content.description:
Sol flagged the stated reason as wrong; I have now REPRODUCED it on the real runtime. Probe: tmp/dirsync-probe.ts.

MEASURED, Bun 1.3.14, win32 arm64 (the actual host-service runtime):
  open(dir,"r")  -> open OK, fsync EPERM
  open(dir,"r+") -> open OK, fsync OK
  open(dir,"a")  -> open OK, fsync OK
  open(dir,"w")  -> open FAILS EISDIR
  fsPromises open(dir,"r+") + handle.sync() -> OK
  r+ immediately after a real tmp->rename in that directory -> fsync OK

THE STATED REASON IS FALSE IN TWO WAYS. crypto.ts:1024-1026 says "Node cannot open a directory handle on win32 (fs.open on a directory fails EISDIR/EPERM)". In fact (a) opening a directory succeeds for r, r+ and a — only `w` gives EISDIR; (b) the EPERM comes from fsync on a READ-ONLY handle, which is precisely the mode the non-win32 path uses (crypto.ts:1048 `open(dir, "r")`). The gap was most likely concluded from trying `r` on Windows, getting EPERM, and generalising.

CONSEQUENCE IF IT HOLDS: syncDirectory need not early-return on win32 (crypto.ts:1047). Renames could be made durable directly, and the cross-file rename-ordering assumption (#22) would stop being load-bearing for BOTH (ATTEMPT-WITNESS) and keys.ts SEND-WITNESS. The witness becomes defence-in-depth rather than the thing correctness rests on. That is a simplification, not more machinery.

WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVEN — do not skip this. A successful fsync call is not evidence that NTFS persisted the directory metadata log. Windows exposes no documented user-space directory-fsync, and Microsoft documents FlushFileBuffers as flushing THE SPECIFIED FILE (a volume handle is required to flush all files); the documented durable-rename primitive is MoveFileEx(MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH), which Node does not surface. So FlushFileBuffers on a directory handle may be a silent no-op that returns success.

REQUIRED BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING:
1. Authoritative documentation on what FlushFileBuffers does for a directory handle on NTFS, or
2. A crash-consistency test (VM hard-reset / power-cut harness) showing a rename survives with the directory fsync and can be lost without it.

A syncDirectory that appears to work but does not would be WORSE than an honest no-op, because every mechanism above it would stop compensating. If the evidence cannot be obtained, the correct outcome is to FIX THE COMMENT's stated reason (it is wrong regardless) while keeping the no-op and the witness.

Related: #22 (the assumption this could retire), #24 (unaffected by this — the lifecycle race is not a durability problem).

content.subject: Short writes (R1), counter saturation (R2), fifth doc site (R3), comment errors (R4)
content.description:
PARTIALLY DONE in 563c41b56.

FIXED:
- R1 writeFileDurable now checks the bytesWritten Node returns and throws before the rename, so a short write can no longer be fsync'd and renamed as though complete (which previously lost every record in the file at the next start, via quarantine).
- R3 the doc-rot list was five sites, not four — all five cleared, plus the harness heading.
- R4 partial: crypto.ts's syncDirectory reason (measurably wrong — a directory opens fine under Bun on win32 arm64 and r+ fsync succeeds; only the read-only mode gives EPERM) is corrected with the measured results and the reason the no-op nonetheless stays. index.ts's teardown-ordering claim is corrected and now true by construction thanks to MAINTENANCE-DRAIN.

STILL OPEN:
- R2 both schemas accept Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER for the rewrite counter while persist() increments it: load ...991 -> write ...992 -> the next increment yields the SAME value -> the following start rejects and quarantines it. Unreachable by human usage, reachable from a schema-valid nonsense file. Bound the schema below MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, or treat saturation as a degrade rather than letting it self-corrupt.
- R4 remainder: answer.ts:1609-1611 says the store never refuses startup — now TRUE after the B1 fix, so re-read it and confirm rather than assume. answer.ts:1726-1728 still claims a failed quarantine rename proves the later durable write would also fail, which an obstruction only at the quarantine destination disproves. The "rise-only" wording still needs scoping: it holds within one store instance and below the numeric boundary, but #24 showed it did not hold across lifecycle overlap (now fixed by the drain) and R2 shows it does not hold at saturation.
- R5 the B1 fix does cover the full error class Sol named (ENOSPC, EACCES, sync/close, failed replacement) because it catches everything raiseWitness can throw rather than matching on codes — worth keeping that way rather than narrowing to specific errno values.

fix(companion): close the attempt store on teardown, check every durable write

The /simplify altitude pass found that my own MAINTENANCE-DRAIN fix from two
commits ago traded a data-corruption bug for a liveness bug, and that the
byte-count check landed in one write site while a worse one went without.

(STORE-CLOSED) The drain was at the wrong altitude and unbounded. `settle`
imposes no timeout and `stop()` runs inside the lifecycle's `exclusive()`, so my
`while (inFlight.size > 0) await Promise.all(...)` meant one `persist` stalled on
a handle held by an antivirus scanner or a search indexer — ordinary transients on
this platform — would hang `stop()` forever, after which no `start()` could ever
run again. A silent permanent wedge is a worse failure than the corruption it
replaced, which at least announced itself at the next mount.

The right guard is on the store, and the codebase already said so: `nonceCache`
and `deviceStore` both refuse work once closed, and `deviceStore`'s debounced
persist is detached and invisible to any drain — `closed` is what protects it. The
attempt store, the one that actually got clobbered, had no `closed`, no `close()`,
and was the ONLY subsystem with no teardown step at all. It now has all three.
The flag is checked inside the serialised section (a rewrite queued while open can
still be in the tail when close lands — that queued write IS the stale writer) and
at the entry to `prune` and `forget`, which mutate memory before they write:
dropping records from the map while refusing the rewrite would make this store's
answers disagree with its own file, and `get` reads the map.

With that guard the drain no longer carries correctness, so it is now bounded at
5s and gives up loudly. Nothing a late task does can reach durable state; the wait
is only about handle lifetime.

writeAll replaces the one-site byte-count check. Three peer paths hand-rolled the
same sequence and did not inherit it, and the sharpest was strictly worse than the
case the check was written for: the replay cache appends FIXED-WIDTH records and
its loader reads from offset 0, trimming only a trailing partial — so a short
append followed by any successful one misaligns the whole remainder of the file,
admitted nonces stop being recognised, and the §3.5 replay window silently
reopens. No error, no schema failure, nothing to notice. Now checked at both
sites through one helper.

Proof: tmp/verify-store-closed.ts — a rewrite racing close() leaves the file and
the counter untouched, prune after close writes nothing and no longer mutates
memory, close() is idempotent, and reads still work (only writes are refused).

Verified: 92/92 markers, 0 companion type diagnostics (8 pre-existing debt
elsewhere unchanged), eight harnesses green including the witness decision table
28/28, and a real bridge boot at 158ms with the witness bound to the live anchor
generation, every hostile probe refused 403 before parsing, and a clean stop.
tmp/companion-crypto-check.ts fails its last two checks against a test-only cap of
4 that violates a production invariant present at HEAD and untouched here; its
"replay rejected after restart" check, which exercises the append path this commit
changes, passes.

Recorded but NOT fixed here, from the same review:
- pending-destroy.json needs rollback protection and has none: the journal's
  rename lands before records are deleted and the index persisted, so losing it
  while the index survives leaves purged devices' K_dev on disk permanently and
  undetectably. The right fix is NOT a third witness — the obligation is
  re-derivable by sweeping for key files whose keyRef is in no index record.
  General principle worth keeping: a witness is only right where the obligation
  cannot be re-derived; where it can, re-derivation dominates.
- the watch can still downgrade a Confirmed answer. QuestionStore.onAnswerResult
  guards identity but not outcome rank, so after a phone process restart the phone
  relays UNKNOWN, the watch maps it to Unconfirmed, and a confirmed answer is
  overwritten on the wrist. The new recordOutcome lattice cannot help — that path
  never enters the phone's answersState. Fix is ~25 lines: rank/supersedes on the
  shared core wire enum, refused non-superseding transitions on both surfaces.

input.description:
From simp-altitude, the most valuable review of the session. Two are real bugs outside tonight's commits; the rest are structural.

A1 (REAL BUG, key leak) pending-destroy.json needs rollback protection and has none. Verified order: writePendingDestroy(merged) at device-store.ts:1078 lands BEFORE records are deleted and the index persisted. Lose the journal's rename while the index's survives -> purged devices are gone from the index, nothing names their keyRefs, and K_dev stays on disk PERMANENTLY and UNDETECTABLY. That is the exact failure device-store.ts:531-535 says this journal replaced. Keys are revoked and tombstoned so nothing is authorised; the cost is a revoked device's key surviving indefinitely, able to decrypt captured historical traffic.
Correct depth is NOT a third witness (crypto.ts forbids another ordering dependent). The obligation is RE-DERIVABLE: sweep at start for key files whose keyRef appears in no index record, reconstructing the list from ground truth with no second file and no ordering assumption. Cost: KeyStore (keys.ts:929-952) has no enumeration, needs list() (~10 lines readdir) plus ~20 lines of sweep in drainPendingDestroy.
PRINCIPLE WORTH KEEPING: a witness is only right where the obligation cannot be re-derived. Where it can, re-derivation strictly dominates.

A2 (REAL BUG, live, user-visible) the watch downgrades a Confirmed answer. QuestionStore.kt:404-440 guards requestId/questionId identity only, never outcome rank, and outstandingRequestId() (:455) returns the id for Confirmed too — so an incoming Unconfirmed for the SAME requestId falls through to else -> applied = true and overwrites Confirmed. Reachable: WatchBridge.kt:309-322, after a phone process restart the phone has no record, relays WatchAnswerStatus.UNKNOWN, the watch maps else -> Unconfirmed (QuestionStore.kt:401), and a confirmed answer is downgraded on the wrist. The new recordOutcome lattice cannot help — it orders only outcomes passing through the phone's answersState and this path never enters it.
Fix (~25 lines): put rank/supersedes on core/wear/WatchAnswerStatus (already in core, so the wire enum is shared while the ordering is not) and have QuestionStore.onAnswerResult refuse a non-superseding incoming, mirroring recordOutcome. Do NOT move AnswerOutcome wholesale to core — it drags phone UI copy (AnswerOutcome.kt:78-94 BridgeErrorCode.userText) along.

A3 (structural, do when a third dependent is proposed) keys.ts:735-848 and answer.ts:1372-1546 are the same machine — rise-only integer beside a durable file, raised before it, generation-bound, max-at-start, gap->verdict — differing only in mark type and verdict severity, which are parameters. crypto.ts already says "do not add a THIRD", which concedes a third is plausible. The ordering invariant is restated as prose in three places and enforced by nothing. Deeper fix: witnessedDurable(path, {generation, onGap}) in crypto.ts putting mark write and file write in ONE function so raise-before-write is structural, ~120 lines net. Factor ONLY the ordering and mark read/write/compare; leave each caller's verdict local, since degrade-vs-throw differ enough that a unified verdict would be a false abstraction.

A4 (extraction, now better motivated) extracting attempt-store.ts is genuinely right, not just moving code: the block (answer.ts:1252-2117, 866 lines of a 3,732-line file) takes EXACTLY ONE identifier from the rest of answer.ts — GUARD_CLASSES, used once as a zod enum key source. The module boundary already exists; the file layout hides it. Cost, all in the SAME commit: move GUARD_CLASSES + GuardClass to types.ts beside AnswerGuardName or attempt-store.ts -> answer.ts closes an IMPORT CYCLE (the earlier review missed this), then update the FEATURES.md (ATTEMPT-WITNESS) marker path or the gate fails.

A5 (doc scope, worse than thought) the win32-rollback rationale is restated in SEVEN production sites, not four: FEATURES.md:78, answer.ts x3, types.ts, PROTOCOL.md, BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:875, Answer.kt:466, plus index.ts and the harness. "not sent" is re-argued 9x in answer.ts and 4x in types.ts. The marker gate genuinely does not generalise — it is grep -rqsF, a presence check; bending it to content equality would fail the build on every wording improvement and train people to edit the gate. Canonical home should be PROTOCOL.md §11.5 (the contract, and the only doc a client author reads). One structural lever IS available: the semantics already have executable copies in AnswerStatusCoverageTest.kt and provesNeverSent — name §11.5 in the test names and treat that file as the second normative copy. Prose-to-behaviour is the one thing a gate cannot give.

A6 (evidence bar) the bar written into crypto.ts for retiring the syncDirectory no-op — an authoritative NTFS statement or a real crash-consistency test — will never be cleared in CI. Consequence to record: both witnesses are PERMANENT, not provisional. And if evidence ever did arrive, KEEP them as defence-in-depth (their detection surface is strictly larger: single-file AV quarantine-restore, per-file version restore, a copied ~/.superset/companion, and generation-bound anchor replacement — a directory fsync sees none of those) but DROP the raise-before-write ordering coupling, which is the fragile half and the only half a working fsync retires.

`/simplify` is complete, and the altitude pass earned its keep — it caught a bug **I introduced two commits earlier**.

**My regression, now fixed.** The `MAINTENANCE-DRAIN` teardown I wrote was unbounded, `settle` has no timeout, and `stop()` runs inside `exclusive()` — so one `persist` stalled on a handle held by an antivirus scanner would hang `stop()` forever and no later `start()` could run. I traded data corruption for a **silent permanent wedge**, which is the worse failure: the corruption at least announced itself at the next mount.

The right guard was one layer down, and the codebase already said so — `nonceCache` and `deviceStore` both refuse work once closed. The attempt store, the one that actually got clobbered, had no `closed`, no `close()`, and was the only subsystem with **no teardown step at all**. Now it has all three, and the drain is bounded at 5s because it no longer carries correctness.

**My other half-fix, completed.** The `bytesWritten` check landed in `writeFileDurable` only, while a worse site went without: the replay cache appends fixed-width records and reads from offset 0, so a short append misaligns the whole remainder of the file — admitted nonces stop being recognised and the **§3.5 replay window silently reopens**. Now checked at both sites through one helper.

My own proof also caught something the fix had missed: `prune` after `close()` mutated memory while refusing to persist, so `get` would report a miss for a record still durably present. Guarded at the entry points too.

Committed `362fc929c`. Boot back to 158ms, 92/92 markers, 0 type errors, eight harnesses green.

**Two real bugs recorded and not fixed tonight** (#27) — both outside this change set, both worth your attention:
- `pending-destroy.json` has no rollback protection, so a revoked device's key can survive on disk permanently and undetectably. The fix is *re-derivation*, not a third witness — and the principle behind that is worth keeping: a witness is only right where the obligation can't be re-derived.
- The **watch can downgrade a `Confirmed` answer** after a phone restart. My new lattice can't help, because that path never enters the phone's state.

Five commits now sit local across both repos, unpushed.

content.content:
1	## Strongest objection
2	
3	I would not ship the actionable “not sent” result yet. It is not linearizable against the original `/answer` request.
4	
5	A valid execution is:
6	
7	1. `/answer` reaches the server but pauses before writing `in_flight`.
8	2. `/status` overtakes it, reads no record, and the client accepts the coverage proof.
9	3. The phone reports “not sent.”
10	4. The original `/answer` resumes, records `in_flight`, and types the answer.
11	
12	The initial lookup happens well before the durable claim in [answer.ts](<C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64/packages/host-service/src/companion/answer.ts:2201>), while status performs an ordinary read in [answer.ts](<C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64/packages/host-service/src/companion/answer.ts:2936>). HTTP cancellation or waiting out the nominal freshness period does not close this race: the server snapshots its freshness time before several awaits in [http.ts](<C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64/packages/host-service/src/companion/http.ts:1119>).
13	
14	The witness can prove something about the past. It cannot prevent a previously admitted request from acting in the future.
15	
16	The required fix is a durable per-request race:
17	
18	| Existing durable state | `/answer` | Authoritative `/status` |
19	|---|---|---|
20	| Absent | CAS to `in_flight` | CAS to `closed_not_received` |
21	| `in_flight` or outcome | Idempotent/duplicate handling | Return known status |
22	| `closed_not_received` | Permanently refuse to type | Return `not_received` |
23	
24	Whichever operation wins is persisted before either typing or returning a terminal negative result. If the status-side CAS cannot be persisted, the result must remain `unconfirmed`.
25	
26	Cost: moderate. It adds a tombstone state, store-level CAS/transaction, one wire outcome, client rendering, and concurrency/crash tests. A non-atomic “check then insert tombstone” is insufficient.
27	
28	## Overall verdict
29

The required fix is a durable per-request race:

| Absent | CAS to `in_flight` | CAS to `closed_not_received` |
| `in_flight` or outcome | Idempotent/duplicate handling | Return known status |

content.subject: Fix five client honest-state findings (F1-F5)
content.description:
From opus-rev-client on f25e438, all verified independently, all PRE-EXISTING rather than regressions. Apply only after every reviewer has reported, to avoid editing files they are reading.

F1 (severe) BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:405-406 — read-back FetchResult.Failure maps to terminal AnswerOutcome.Failed, violating §11.6. Blast radius: :453 overwrites a stored Confirmed with Failed; QuestionSheet.kt:542-570 renders Failed as terminal and removes the resolve affordance; WatchBridge.kt:514-520 relays FAILED while app-watch's own failed-read path correctly keeps unconfirmed. Fix: map read failure to Unconfirmed; reserve Failed for status=="failed".

F2 BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:417-421 and :365-369 — confirmed/absent resolvedAtMs yields Failed(INTERNAL). Should be Unconfirmed.

F3 Answer.kt:430-433 — questionId/resolvedAtMs/failureCode are nullable without `= null` defaults, so an omitted key throws ProtocolException and lands in F1's path. The three new proof fields do have defaults; the asymmetry is the defect.

F4 Answer.kt:506-511 — provesNeverSent ignores status, so known:false + in_flight still licenses "not sent". Guard: require status in {UNKNOWN, UNCONFIRMED}.

F5 Answer.kt:473-480 — no plausibility bound on the claimed window; bounded to 24h only incidentally by the retention gate. Cap coverageAgeMs at ATTEMPT_RECORD_RETENTION_MS to make it structural.

F6 (mine, contract review) PROTOCOL.md §11.5 degrade-case list omits "no install generation supplied", though it reads as exhaustive. Production cannot reach it (openStateAnchor throws unless the generation is canonical) but the list should be complete.

VERIFIED CLEAN, do not re-investigate: field names/casing/types/units match exactly both sides; comparison strictness is `>` in client, PROTOCOL.md:1670 and types.ts:986; retention 86_400_000 both sides with an independent server clamp; no surviving trace in either repo of the corrected false claim about `confirmed` surviving restarts; elapsedRealtime cannot yield a too-small submitAgeMs (writeLifetimes is process-scoped, a reboot kills the holder); partial proof-field sets decline correctly; app-watch has no duplicate decision.

content.subject: Fix witness-write throw (B1) and unwitnessed-advance belief (C2)
content.description:
B1 FIXED and verified (563c41b56): raiseWitness wrapped, degrades on any write fault, proven through the write path specifically by tmp/verify-b1-fix.ts (a directory at the witness path fails on READ first and proves nothing; the probe puts a directory at the .tmp name instead so reads succeed and writes fail). Continuing after the degrade is safe because degradeCoverage advances coverageSinceMs before `file` is built.

C2 STILL OPEN. After a generation-less mount whose witness unlink fails, the file advances unwitnessed while a stale witness stays behind it; a later good mount reads "witness behind file" as the harmless direction and believes the stamp. Reproduced twice independently (opus-rev-server's tmp/review-witness-holes.ts case C2, and Sol with a real Windows deny-delete lock).

Why it is still open rather than fixed: it requires a generation-null mount, and the only production caller (index.ts) passes anchor.generation, which openStateAnchor guarantees is canonical or throws. The D5 fix (generation is now `string | null`, required) makes an accidental omission a compile error, which removes the realistic route in. Residual needs a wiring regression PLUS an unlink failure PLUS a hard reset.

Hardening option if it is ever wanted, from fable-rev-durability: have a generation-null mount freeze the file's seq at 0, or write a tombstone-generation witness, so the next good mount sees witness-ahead or a generation mismatch and degrades instead of trusting. A write survives a Windows sharing violation more often than a delete does, which is the argument for the tombstone over the unlink.

content.subject: Clamp the coverage window against a forward desktop clock step (H3)
content.description:
From fable-rev-honesty, PLAUSIBLE but the consequence is the unrecoverable one. Distinct from D6 (which is about pruned records and is bounded by the client contract); this one produces the actual user-visible lie.

H3: the "ages not wall clocks" design only cancels PHONE-vs-DESKTOP skew. coverageAgeMs = serverTimeMs - recordsSinceMs is a wall-clock difference taken across time on ONE machine (both from Date.now() on the desktop), so a FORWARD step of the desktop clock between coverage start and the query inflates the claimed window by the step size.

Scenario: hard reset rolls the attempts file back and records are lost -> witness degrades, coverage = mount instant (wall clock). Desktop clock then corrects forward 1h (NTP fixing a slow clock, or a user time change). The user's answer landed 40 min ago, pre-crash, and its record was lost. Client computes submitAgeMs 40min < coverageAgeMs ~1h -> provesNeverSent -> user is told "the desktop never saw this request — it was not sent" for an answer that landed -> re-answers the picker -> §11.4 unrecoverable.

Exposure is confined to the coverage=mount (degraded) cases, because a witness-verified window implies no record loss and those windows are retention-floored. That is what makes it clampable.

Fix options: (a) server-side, when degraded, publish recordsSinceMs such that coverageAgeMs <= monotonic elapsed since mount (anchor on process.hrtime rather than Date.now()); or (b) client-side, cap proof 1 with proof 2's lifetime bracket. (a) is better — it fixes the claim at the source rather than making every client compensate.

Backward steps are already safe: recordsSinceMs > serverTimeMs -> coverageAgeMs null -> Unconfirmed, and that is already tested.

Note the shared root with D6: both are Date.now() being treated as monotonic. A single fix — anchoring published instants to a monotonic source — may close both. Consider that before fixing them separately.

content.subject: Witness durability rests on an undocumented rename-ordering assumption
content.description:
From sol-contract (GPT-5.6 Sol, ultra). This questions the premise the whole mechanism rests on, and the same premise underpins keys.ts SEND-WITNESS.

THE CLAIM (crypto.ts:1046, answer.ts:1410, answer.ts:1942): the witness write is made durable by the ATTEMPTS file's subsequent content fsync, because the witness's rename record sits in the same directory metadata log that the fsync flushes.

SOL'S OBJECTION: Microsoft documents FlushFileBuffers as flushing THE SPECIFIED FILE, and states a volume handle is required to flush all files on a volume. MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH exists as a SEPARATE, explicit move-durability guarantee, and Node exposes no equivalent durable-rename option. So "F's fsync publishes W's rename" is an incidental filesystem ordering assumption, not a documented guarantee.

IF IT IS WRONG: witness W and attempts file F can both roll back to a matching version n-1. The next mount then sees EQUAL counters, logs no degradation, has lost the record, and publishes the old coverage — and the client reports a landed answer as "never sent". That is the exact failure the witness was built to prevent, and it would be invisible.

EVIDENCE STATUS, stated honestly by Sol: it restored both pre-write files and reproduced known:false with zero degradation events and a true client age comparison — i.e. the POSTCONDITION is confirmed harmful. Whether a real NTFS hard reset can actually produce that joint rollback is REASONED, not power-cut reproduced.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THIS COMMIT: keys.ts's SEND-WITNESS relies on the identical assumption for send-nonce anti-rollback, where the consequence is AES-GCM nonce reuse. If the assumption is unsound, that mechanism is weaker than its comments claim too — though it fails closed (refuses to start) rather than lying.

WHAT TO DO — do not silently "fix" this, it needs a decision:
(a) Get authoritative evidence: a documented NTFS/Windows guarantee, or a real crash-consistency test (power-cut / VM reset harness), or
(b) Weaken the comments to state it as a best-effort ordering assumption rather than a proof, and say what is NOT covered, or
(c) Find a construction that does not depend on cross-file rename ordering at all — e.g. put the counter INSIDE the attempts file plus a separate append-only (never renamed) witness log, since append+fsync has no rename to lose. Note the replay cache is already structurally immune for exactly this reason (append+fsync per admit, rename only at compaction where a lost rename reverts to a SUPERSET = conservative).

Option (c) is the only one that removes the doubt rather than documenting it.

content.subject: Sol findings: clock (S1), lifetime aliasing (S2), in_flight polling (S3), boundary validation (S4)
content.description:
From sol-contract (ultra). Items not already tracked in #18-#21.

S1 (CONFIRMED, upgrades H3/D6 from plausible to reproduced) Sol reproduced the clock defect end-to-end with the real store and handler, and its scenario is better than the one I recorded: a landed record is 23 REAL hours old; the desktop clock jumps forward 2h; prune sees 25h and deletes it; the server advertises a 24h coverage age while the phone measures ~23h; 24h > 23h -> "never sent". Measured: record absent, degradation events none, coverageAgeMs 86,400,000, monotonic submit age 60,000, client predicate TRUE. This merges D6 (#20) and H3 (#21) into ONE confirmed defect: wall time treated as monotonic. Fix at the source with a monotonic anchor.

S2 (NEW) bridgeStartedMs is only Date.now() (index.ts:323) but the client treats equality as exact lifetime IDENTITY (BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:88). Repeated wall time can alias two different bridge lifetimes, making the fallback proof unsafe. Fix: mint a per-lifetime random/monotonic id, or combine Date.now() with the install generation + a counter.

S3 (NEW, medium) `in_flight` is never re-polled. The server durably records in_flight before typing (answer.ts:2383) and the repository correctly maps it to Pending (BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:431), but the phone performs exactly one status read, "never in a loop" (ConversationViewModel.kt:383), and the watch converts Pending to unknown (WatchBridge.kt:529). PROTOCOL.md:1721 and :1732 REQUIRE pending display and continued polling. Scenario: the status read lands during the ~15s injection window; the server later records confirmed; the phone stays Pending until the user intervenes and the watch shows Unconfirmed. Either implement bounded polling or change the spec — but they must agree.

S4 (NEW, medium) No cross-field or echoed-id validation at either boundary. The server's untrusted-disk schema validates fields independently (answer.ts:1314) and emits them unchanged (answer.ts:2948), so it will happily serve `confirmed` with `resolvedAtMs: null`. Per NON-NEGOTIABLE RULE 1 the SERVER should reject that shape at its own disk boundary, not just have the client cope (which is F2). Separately the client never checks the echoed requestId (Answer.kt:425, BridgeClient.kt:246), so a future erroneous response for request B could settle A — currently unreachable because response AAD binds the request nonce.

S5 (NEW, low) PROTOCOL §11.5 (PROTOCOL.md:1645) declares the proof fields required and non-null, while the Kotlin serializer coerces missing, null, fractional, quoted, object, boolean and overflow values to null (Answer.kt:385). Missing fields NEED that exception for old-server compatibility, but the spec does not say so — and coercing MALFORMED values contradicts §0's hard-error rule. Decide which rule wins and make both sides state it.

S6 The false "witness preserves confirmed after restart" claim also survives in the harness itself, tmp/attempt-witness-proof.ts:70 — so the fix list for D1 is five sites, not four.

S7 The retention constant can drift silently: no shared vector or cross-repo assertion covers it. Consider adding it to the differential vector set, which already crosses the language boundary.

CONFIRMED CLEAN by Sol, agreeing with earlier passes: all nine JSON keys/casing/status spellings/units align; the server always emits all three proof fields on both branches; strict `>` in spec, server docs, client and tests; negative/reversed/absent/half windows conservatively lose proof; a degraded window is correct while the wall clock stays continuous; known:true responses are unaffected by degradation; all three compatibility directions are safe.

content.subject: CRITICAL: detached prune from a stopped store clobbers the new store and lowers the counter
content.description:
From sol-crash-consistency (GPT-5.6 Sol ultra, EXECUTED with a probe against the real implementation). This is the most severe finding of the entire review: it needs no filesystem assumption, no clock step, and no wiring fault — just a stop/start while an hourly prune is in flight.

MECHANISM (verified by me): index.ts:654-657 fires `interval(HOUR_MS, async () => { await attempts.prune(Date.now()); ... })`. Teardown (index.ts:685-689) only does `clearInterval(timer)` — it NEVER awaits an in-flight callback. So a prune already executing when the bridge stops keeps a live reference to the OLD AttemptStore closure (its records map, its seq, its paths). Serialization and the witness read/write guard are per-INSTANCE only (answer.ts:1892-1967), so the old instance's persist() has no idea a new instance exists.

SEQUENCE (Sol's probe output): old store at F/W=2 begins prune and reads W=2 -> stop/start creates a new store which reaches F/W=3, then records an answer at F/W=4 -> the old prune resumes and writes its stale empty snapshot as W=3, F=3. Measured: before releasing the old prune F=4/W=4 records [old,new]; after F=3/W=3 records []; on reopen no degradation, the new record absent, old coverage retained. The next restart therefore TRUSTS a matching pair while a recorded answer has been destroyed -> false "it was not sent".

THIS BREAKS THE RISE-ONLY CLAIM. I verified rise-only within one instance and reported it as holding; it does not hold across instances. Math.max and the promise tail cannot see another instance's writes.

BROADER CLASS: the same detached-interval pattern covers nonceCache.compact, audit.prune and deviceStore.purgeExpiredRevocations in the same block. Check whether any of those can also clobber a successor's state. The nonce cache is the one to look at hardest, since its rollback consequence is the fatal one.

FIX DIRECTIONS: (a) make teardown await in-flight maintenance, not just clear timers — track the in-flight promise and await it in the unwind entry; (b) give each store instance an ownership token and have persist() refuse if it is no longer the owner (the anchor already has this shape for the send-nonce lifecycle); (c) both. (b) defends even against a leaked reference that outlives teardown.

Also from the same report, comment errors this invalidates: index.ts:699-704 and 723-724 claim teardown prevents old writers overlapping a new bridge — detached maintenance makes that false. And answer.ts:1457 / 1877-1882 claim witness-ahead PROVES an attempts-file version was durably written and then lost; a failure between the witness raise and the primary write produces the identical state with no such version ever existing.

content.subject: Lead: an r+ directory handle may be fsync-able on Windows, which would retire the ordering assumption
content.description:
Sol flagged the stated reason as wrong; I have now REPRODUCED it on the real runtime. Probe: tmp/dirsync-probe.ts.

MEASURED, Bun 1.3.14, win32 arm64 (the actual host-service runtime):
  open(dir,"r")  -> open OK, fsync EPERM
  open(dir,"r+") -> open OK, fsync OK
  open(dir,"a")  -> open OK, fsync OK
  open(dir,"w")  -> open FAILS EISDIR
  fsPromises open(dir,"r+") + handle.sync() -> OK
  r+ immediately after a real tmp->rename in that directory -> fsync OK

THE STATED REASON IS FALSE IN TWO WAYS. crypto.ts:1024-1026 says "Node cannot open a directory handle on win32 (fs.open on a directory fails EISDIR/EPERM)". In fact (a) opening a directory succeeds for r, r+ and a — only `w` gives EISDIR; (b) the EPERM comes from fsync on a READ-ONLY handle, which is precisely the mode the non-win32 path uses (crypto.ts:1048 `open(dir, "r")`). The gap was most likely concluded from trying `r` on Windows, getting EPERM, and generalising.

CONSEQUENCE IF IT HOLDS: syncDirectory need not early-return on win32 (crypto.ts:1047). Renames could be made durable directly, and the cross-file rename-ordering assumption (#22) would stop being load-bearing for BOTH (ATTEMPT-WITNESS) and keys.ts SEND-WITNESS. The witness becomes defence-in-depth rather than the thing correctness rests on. That is a simplification, not more machinery.

WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVEN — do not skip this. A successful fsync call is not evidence that NTFS persisted the directory metadata log. Windows exposes no documented user-space directory-fsync, and Microsoft documents FlushFileBuffers as flushing THE SPECIFIED FILE (a volume handle is required to flush all files); the documented durable-rename primitive is MoveFileEx(MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH), which Node does not surface. So FlushFileBuffers on a directory handle may be a silent no-op that returns success.

REQUIRED BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING:
1. Authoritative documentation on what FlushFileBuffers does for a directory handle on NTFS, or
2. A crash-consistency test (VM hard-reset / power-cut harness) showing a rename survives with the directory fsync and can be lost without it.

A syncDirectory that appears to work but does not would be WORSE than an honest no-op, because every mechanism above it would stop compensating. If the evidence cannot be obtained, the correct outcome is to FIX THE COMMENT's stated reason (it is wrong regardless) while keeping the no-op and the witness.

Related: #22 (the assumption this could retire), #24 (unaffected by this — the lifecycle race is not a durability problem).

content.subject: Short writes (R1), counter saturation (R2), fifth doc site (R3), comment errors (R4)
content.description:
PARTIALLY DONE in 563c41b56.

FIXED:
- R1 writeFileDurable now checks the bytesWritten Node returns and throws before the rename, so a short write can no longer be fsync'd and renamed as though complete (which previously lost every record in the file at the next start, via quarantine).
- R3 the doc-rot list was five sites, not four — all five cleared, plus the harness heading.
- R4 partial: crypto.ts's syncDirectory reason (measurably wrong — a directory opens fine under Bun on win32 arm64 and r+ fsync succeeds; only the read-only mode gives EPERM) is corrected with the measured results and the reason the no-op nonetheless stays. index.ts's teardown-ordering claim is corrected and now true by construction thanks to MAINTENANCE-DRAIN.

STILL OPEN:
- R2 both schemas accept Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER for the rewrite counter while persist() increments it: load ...991 -> write ...992 -> the next increment yields the SAME value -> the following start rejects and quarantines it. Unreachable by human usage, reachable from a schema-valid nonsense file. Bound the schema below MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, or treat saturation as a degrade rather than letting it self-corrupt.
- R4 remainder: answer.ts:1609-1611 says the store never refuses startup — now TRUE after the B1 fix, so re-read it and confirm rather than assume. answer.ts:1726-1728 still claims a failed quarantine rename proves the later durable write would also fail, which an obstruction only at the quarantine destination disproves. The "rise-only" wording still needs scoping: it holds within one store instance and below the numeric boundary, but #24 showed it did not hold across lifecycle overlap (now fixed by the drain) and R2 shows it does not hold at saturation.
- R5 the B1 fix does cover the full error class Sol named (ENOSPC, EACCES, sync/close, failed replacement) because it catches everything raiseWitness can throw rather than matching on codes — worth keeping that way rather than narrowing to specific errno values.

content.subject: Altitude findings: pending-destroy key leak (A1), watch Confirmed downgrade (A2), witness factoring (A3)
content.description:
From simp-altitude, the most valuable review of the session. Two are real bugs outside tonight's commits; the rest are structural.

A1 (REAL BUG, key leak) pending-destroy.json needs rollback protection and has none. Verified order: writePendingDestroy(merged) at device-store.ts:1078 lands BEFORE records are deleted and the index persisted. Lose the journal's rename while the index's survives -> purged devices are gone from the index, nothing names their keyRefs, and K_dev stays on disk PERMANENTLY and UNDETECTABLY. That is the exact failure device-store.ts:531-535 says this journal replaced. Keys are revoked and tombstoned so nothing is authorised; the cost is a revoked device's key surviving indefinitely, able to decrypt captured historical traffic.
Correct depth is NOT a third witness (crypto.ts forbids another ordering dependent). The obligation is RE-DERIVABLE: sweep at start for key files whose keyRef appears in no index record, reconstructing the list from ground truth with no second file and no ordering assumption. Cost: KeyStore (keys.ts:929-952) has no enumeration, needs list() (~10 lines readdir) plus ~20 lines of sweep in drainPendingDestroy.
PRINCIPLE WORTH KEEPING: a witness is only right where the obligation cannot be re-derived. Where it can, re-derivation strictly dominates.

A2 (REAL BUG, live, user-visible) the watch downgrades a Confirmed answer. QuestionStore.kt:404-440 guards requestId/questionId identity only, never outcome rank, and outstandingRequestId() (:455) returns the id for Confirmed too — so an incoming Unconfirmed for the SAME requestId falls through to else -> applied = true and overwrites Confirmed. Reachable: WatchBridge.kt:309-322, after a phone process restart the phone has no record, relays WatchAnswerStatus.UNKNOWN, the watch maps else -> Unconfirmed (QuestionStore.kt:401), and a confirmed answer is downgraded on the wrist. The new recordOutcome lattice cannot help — it orders only outcomes passing through the phone's answersState and this path never enters it.
Fix (~25 lines): put rank/supersedes on core/wear/WatchAnswerStatus (already in core, so the wire enum is shared while the ordering is not) and have QuestionStore.onAnswerResult refuse a non-superseding incoming, mirroring recordOutcome. Do NOT move AnswerOutcome wholesale to core — it drags phone UI copy (AnswerOutcome.kt:78-94 BridgeErrorCode.userText) along.

A3 (structural, do when a third dependent is proposed) keys.ts:735-848 and answer.ts:1372-1546 are the same machine — rise-only integer beside a durable file, raised before it, generation-bound, max-at-start, gap->verdict — differing only in mark type and verdict severity, which are parameters. crypto.ts already says "do not add a THIRD", which concedes a third is plausible. The ordering invariant is restated as prose in three places and enforced by nothing. Deeper fix: witnessedDurable(path, {generation, onGap}) in crypto.ts putting mark write and file write in ONE function so raise-before-write is structural, ~120 lines net. Factor ONLY the ordering and mark read/write/compare; leave each caller's verdict local, since degrade-vs-throw differ enough that a unified verdict would be a false abstraction.

A4 (extraction, now better motivated) extracting attempt-store.ts is genuinely right, not just moving code: the block (answer.ts:1252-2117, 866 lines of a 3,732-line file) takes EXACTLY ONE identifier from the rest of answer.ts — GUARD_CLASSES, used once as a zod enum key source. The module boundary already exists; the file layout hides it. Cost, all in the SAME commit: move GUARD_CLASSES + GuardClass to types.ts beside AnswerGuardName or attempt-store.ts -> answer.ts closes an IMPORT CYCLE (the earlier review missed this), then update the FEATURES.md (ATTEMPT-WITNESS) marker path or the gate fails.

A5 (doc scope, worse than thought) the win32-rollback rationale is restated in SEVEN production sites, not four: FEATURES.md:78, answer.ts x3, types.ts, PROTOCOL.md, BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:875, Answer.kt:466, plus index.ts and the harness. "not sent" is re-argued 9x in answer.ts and 4x in types.ts. The marker gate genuinely does not generalise — it is grep -rqsF, a presence check; bending it to content equality would fail the build on every wording improvement and train people to edit the gate. Canonical home should be PROTOCOL.md §11.5 (the contract, and the only doc a client author reads). One structural lever IS available: the semantics already have executable copies in AnswerStatusCoverageTest.kt and provesNeverSent — name §11.5 in the test names and treat that file as the second normative copy. Prose-to-behaviour is the one thing a gate cannot give.

A6 (evidence bar) the bar written into crypto.ts for retiring the syncDirectory no-op — an authoritative NTFS statement or a real crash-consistency test — will never be cleared in CI. Consequence to record: both witnesses are PERMANENT, not provisional. And if evidence ever did arrive, KEEP them as defence-in-depth (their detection surface is strictly larger: single-file AV quarantine-restore, per-file version restore, a copied ~/.superset/companion, and generation-bound anchor replacement — a directory fsync sees none of those) but DROP the raise-before-write ordering coupling, which is the fragile half and the only half a working fsync retires.

content.text:
Race confirmed: the lookup sits at `answer.ts:2309`, the durable `in_flight` claim at `2504` — 195 lines and several awaits apart. A `/status` arriving in that window sees no record and, with a valid coverage window, licenses a terminal "not sent" for an answer that is about to be typed.

That makes the *actionable negative* unsound as built, independent of the witness. Sol's read is right: positive statuses can ship, absence must not be terminal until a durable rejection fence exists. Splitting the remaining work three ways.

input.description: Fix pending-destroy key leak
input.name: fix-keyleak
input.prompt:
Fix a durable-state gap that can leave a revoked device's encryption key on disk permanently and undetectably. Repo: `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64` ONLY, and within it ONLY `packages/host-service/src/companion/device-store.ts` and `keys.ts`. I am concurrently editing `answer.ts` and `index.ts` in the same directory — do not touch those two, or `crypto.ts`.

## The gap (found by an architectural review, verify it yourself first)

`device-store.ts` keeps `pending-destroy.json`, a journal naming the `keyRef`s whose key files must still be deleted. Around `device-store.ts:1078`, `writePendingDestroy(merged)` lands BEFORE the records are deleted from the index and the index is persisted.

On win32 `syncDirectory` is a no-op (see the comment on it in `crypto.ts`), so a hard reset can lose one file's most recent rename. Lose the JOURNAL's rename while the INDEX's survives and you get: purged devices gone from the index, nothing left naming their `keyRef`s, and `K_dev` sitting on disk permanently with nothing that will ever come back for it. The comment around `device-store.ts:531-535` describes that exact failure as the thing this journal was introduced to prevent.

Consequence to be precise about: the keys are revoked and tombstoned, so nothing is AUTHORISED by this. The cost is a revoked device's key surviving indefinitely and remaining able to decrypt captured historical traffic.

## The fix — re-derivation, NOT a third witness

Do NOT add another witness file. `crypto.ts` explicitly says not to add a third dependent on its cross-file rename ordering, and that ordering is itself an undocumented assumption.

The obligation here is RE-DERIVABLE from ground truth: a key file whose `keyRef` appears in no index record is an orphan and must be destroyed, whatever the journal says. That needs no second file and no ordering assumption.

Implement:
1. An enumeration on `KeyStore` (around `keys.ts:929-952`, which currently has none) — roughly a `readdir` filtered to the key-file suffix, returning `keyRef`s. Keep it in the style of the surrounding code.
2. An orphan sweep, run where `drainPendingDestroy` already runs, that unions the journal's list with `keyRefs on disk MINUS keyRefs present in the index` and destroys the union.

The general principle, worth stating in a comment because it generalises: **a witness is only right where the obligation cannot be re-derived; where it can, re-derivation strictly dominates** — it needs no second file, no write ordering, and no crash-consistency assumption.

## Constraints

- Fail loud, never silently: if enumeration or a delete fails, log structurally with enough to act on. Do not swallow.
- A sweep must never destroy a key still referenced by a live index record. That is the one direction that would be catastrophic — get the set arithmetic right and make the safe direction obvious to a reader.
- Consider and state what happens on a FRESH install (no key files, no index) and on a legacy install — neither should log a phantom fault.
- Match the file's existing comment density; this codebase explains WHY at length and the reasoning is load-bearing.
- Do not touch `FEATURES.md`, `scripts/`, build files, `bun.lock`.
- Do not commit.

## Verify

From Git Bash in the fork root:
```
cd packages/host-service && bunx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -c "src/companion/"   # must be 0
cd ../.. && node scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs                              # 92
bun ./tmp/boot-bridge.ts                                                        # real bridge boot, must still start
```
`bun ./tmp/x.ts`, never `bun run tmp/x.ts`. Piping through `tail`/`grep` masks exit codes. `bunx tsc` reports 8 PRE-EXISTING diagnostics outside `src/companion/` — those are accepted debt; zero INSIDE `src/companion/` is the bar.

Write a probe under `tmp/` proving the sweep: construct a store, pair a device, revoke and purge it, simulate the lost journal rename (delete or revert `pending-destroy.json`) while leaving the index persisted, reopen, and show the orphaned key file is destroyed. Also prove a referenced key is NOT destroyed.

Report the diff, the set arithmetic you chose and why it is safe, the fresh/legacy behaviour, and verbatim gate output. If you conclude the gap is not real or the fix is wrong, say so plainly rather than implementing it badly.

Do NOT add another witness file. `crypto.ts` explicitly says not to add a third dependent on its cross-file rename ordering, and that ordering is itself an undocumented assumption.

The obligation here is RE-DERIVABLE from ground truth: a key file whose `keyRef` appears in no index record is an orphan and must be destroyed, whatever the journal says. That needs no second file and no ordering assumption.

1. An enumeration on `KeyStore` (around `keys.ts:929-952`, which currently has none) — roughly a `readdir` filtered to the key-file suffix, returning `keyRef`s. Keep it in the style of the surrounding code.
2. An orphan sweep, run where `drainPendingDestroy` already runs, that unions the journal's list with `keyRefs on disk MINUS keyRefs present in the index` and destroys the union.

- A sweep must never destroy a key still referenced by a live index record. That is the one direction that would be catastrophic — get the set arithmetic right and make the safe direction obvious to a reader.

- Match the file's existing comment density; this codebase explains WHY at length and the reasoning is load-bearing.
- Do not touch `FEATURES.md`, `scripts/`, build files, `bun.lock`.
- Do not commit.

Two fixes in the Kotlin companion app. Repo: `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion` ONLY — do not touch the sibling fork repo, I am editing it concurrently.

Read `PROTOCOL.md` §11.4, §11.5, §11.6 first. Context: the app answers a blocked AI agent's multiple-choice question from a phone or watch; a desktop bridge types the keystrokes. Telling the user an answer failed or was never sent, when it landed, makes them answer twice — §11.4 records that as unrecoverable.

## FIX 1 — the watch downgrades a Confirmed answer (live, user-visible)

`app-watch/.../state/QuestionStore.kt` around `:404-440`: `onAnswerResult` guards on requestId/questionId IDENTITY only, never on outcome RANK. And `outstandingRequestId()` (~`:455`) returns the id for `Confirmed` too. So an incoming `Unconfirmed` for the SAME requestId falls through to `else -> applied = true` and OVERWRITES a `Confirmed`.

Reachable path, not hypothetical: `app-phone/.../wear/WatchBridge.kt:309-322` — after a phone process restart the phone has no record of the request, relays `WatchAnswerStatus.UNKNOWN`, the watch maps `else -> Unconfirmed` (~`QuestionStore.kt:401`), and a confirmed answer is downgraded on the wrist.

The phone already got a monotonicity lattice for this (`BridgeCompanionRepository.recordOutcome` / `supersedes`, ~`:1018-1034`: Confirmed is terminal, Failed yields only to Confirmed, Pending and Unconfirmed yield to anything). It cannot help here — it orders only outcomes passing through the phone's `answersState`, and this path never enters it.

Fix at the shared layer, cheaply: put `rank`/`supersedes` on `core/.../wear/WatchAnswerStatus` (already in `core/`, so the wire enum is shared while the ordering is not) and have `QuestionStore.onAnswerResult` refuse a non-superseding incoming, mirroring the phone's rule. Keep ONE ordering both surfaces bind to.

Do NOT move `AnswerOutcome` wholesale into `core/` — it drags phone UI copy along (`AnswerOutcome.kt:78-94` `BridgeErrorCode.userText`) and is a much larger change for no extra safety.

## FIX 2 — a proven-absence verdict must stop being terminal

This is the more important one and it REMOVES a capability on purpose.

`Answer.kt`'s `provesNeverSent` plus `BridgeCompanionRepository.unknownRequestOutcome` currently turn a missing record inside the server's coverage window into a terminal `Failed(TRANSPORT, "the desktop never saw this request — it was not sent")`.

That inference is unsound, and not because of anything on the client. An architectural review found the server race and I verified it: `handleAnswer` looks up the attempt record at `answer.ts:2309` and does not durably record `in_flight` until `answer.ts:2504` — 195 lines and several awaits later, including guard evaluation and lock acquisition. So a `/v1/answer/status` read that OVERTAKES an already-admitted `/v1/answer` sees no record, the coverage proof holds, the phone says "not sent" — and then the original request resumes and TYPES the answer. The server's coverage window is an honest claim about the PAST; it cannot promise that an admitted request will not act in the FUTURE. Closing it properly needs a durable compare-and-set with a `closed_not_received` tombstone on the server, which does not exist yet.

So: while there is no durable rejection fence, proven absence must resolve to `Unconfirmed`, not to any terminal outcome. Keep the whole coverage-proof machinery and its tests — the arithmetic is correct and will be needed again — but make the VERDICT non-terminal, and make the reason explicit in the code so nobody re-enables it without the fence. State plainly in the comment that this is a deliberate capability regression pending a server-side CAS, not a bug.

Positive stored statuses are unaffected: `known: true` still returns the record's own status, including `Confirmed`. Only the inference from ABSENCE changes.

## Constraints

- Every outcome state stays distinct and means exactly what it says. Weakening a claim is safe; strengthening it is the bug.
- Do NOT touch `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, build files, `local.properties`, `keystore/`. Add no dependencies.
- Match the surrounding comment density — this codebase explains WHY at length.
- Do not commit.

## Verify

```
cd "C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/superset-companion"
export JAVA_HOME="C:/Users/khair/dev-tools/jdk-21"; export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
./gradlew assembleDebug --console=plain
./gradlew :core:testDebugUnitTest --console=plain --tests '*AnswerStatusCoverageTest'
```
Currently BUILD SUCCESSFUL and 23/23. Both must still pass. Existing tests asserting a terminal "not sent" will now be wrong — UPDATE them to assert `Unconfirmed`, and record in a comment what they used to assert and why it changed. Do not delete the coverage-arithmetic tests.

Add tests for FIX 1: an `Unconfirmed` arriving for a requestId already `Confirmed` must not downgrade it, and the UNKNOWN-after-phone-restart relay path specifically.

Do NOT run a bare `:core:testDebugUnitTest` and report a failure — `CrossRuntimeDifferentialVectors20260729Test` deliberately throws without `SC_KOTLIN_VECTOR_FILE` and runs via its own harness.

Report both diffs, which tests you added or changed and why, and verbatim build output.

content.subject: Fix five client honest-state findings (F1-F5)
content.description:
From opus-rev-client on f25e438, all verified independently, all PRE-EXISTING rather than regressions. Apply only after every reviewer has reported, to avoid editing files they are reading.

F1 (severe) BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:405-406 — read-back FetchResult.Failure maps to terminal AnswerOutcome.Failed, violating §11.6. Blast radius: :453 overwrites a stored Confirmed with Failed; QuestionSheet.kt:542-570 renders Failed as terminal and removes the resolve affordance; WatchBridge.kt:514-520 relays FAILED while app-watch's own failed-read path correctly keeps unconfirmed. Fix: map read failure to Unconfirmed; reserve Failed for status=="failed".

F2 BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:417-421 and :365-369 — confirmed/absent resolvedAtMs yields Failed(INTERNAL). Should be Unconfirmed.

F3 Answer.kt:430-433 — questionId/resolvedAtMs/failureCode are nullable without `= null` defaults, so an omitted key throws ProtocolException and lands in F1's path. The three new proof fields do have defaults; the asymmetry is the defect.

F4 Answer.kt:506-511 — provesNeverSent ignores status, so known:false + in_flight still licenses "not sent". Guard: require status in {UNKNOWN, UNCONFIRMED}.

F5 Answer.kt:473-480 — no plausibility bound on the claimed window; bounded to 24h only incidentally by the retention gate. Cap coverageAgeMs at ATTEMPT_RECORD_RETENTION_MS to make it structural.

F6 (mine, contract review) PROTOCOL.md §11.5 degrade-case list omits "no install generation supplied", though it reads as exhaustive. Production cannot reach it (openStateAnchor throws unless the generation is canonical) but the list should be complete.

VERIFIED CLEAN, do not re-investigate: field names/casing/types/units match exactly both sides; comparison strictness is `>` in client, PROTOCOL.md:1670 and types.ts:986; retention 86_400_000 both sides with an independent server clamp; no surviving trace in either repo of the corrected false claim about `confirmed` surviving restarts; elapsedRealtime cannot yield a too-small submitAgeMs (writeLifetimes is process-scoped, a reboot kills the holder); partial proof-field sets decline correctly; app-watch has no duplicate decision.

content.subject: Fix witness-write throw (B1) and unwitnessed-advance belief (C2)
content.description:
B1 FIXED and verified (563c41b56): raiseWitness wrapped, degrades on any write fault, proven through the write path specifically by tmp/verify-b1-fix.ts (a directory at the witness path fails on READ first and proves nothing; the probe puts a directory at the .tmp name instead so reads succeed and writes fail). Continuing after the degrade is safe because degradeCoverage advances coverageSinceMs before `file` is built.

C2 STILL OPEN. After a generation-less mount whose witness unlink fails, the file advances unwitnessed while a stale witness stays behind it; a later good mount reads "witness behind file" as the harmless direction and believes the stamp. Reproduced twice independently (opus-rev-server's tmp/review-witness-holes.ts case C2, and Sol with a real Windows deny-delete lock).

Why it is still open rather than fixed: it requires a generation-null mount, and the only production caller (index.ts) passes anchor.generation, which openStateAnchor guarantees is canonical or throws. The D5 fix (generation is now `string | null`, required) makes an accidental omission a compile error, which removes the realistic route in. Residual needs a wiring regression PLUS an unlink failure PLUS a hard reset.

Hardening option if it is ever wanted, from fable-rev-durability: have a generation-null mount freeze the file's seq at 0, or write a tombstone-generation witness, so the next good mount sees witness-ahead or a generation mismatch and degrades instead of trusting. A write survives a Windows sharing violation more often than a delete does, which is the argument for the tombstone over the unlink.

content.subject: Fix doc rot (D1-D4), generation optionality (D5), prune/clock invariant (D6)
content.description:
PARTIALLY DONE in 563c41b56. Remaining work is D6 only.

FIXED and verified:
- D1 all five copies of the false "witness keeps a landed answer reading confirmed across a restart" claim in answer.ts (1335, 1386, 1600, the createAttemptStore generation doc, and the handleAnswerStatus header), plus the tmp/attempt-witness-proof.ts case-1 heading that repeated it. Multiline grep confirms none remain in source.
- D1b answer.ts:2889-2893 no longer states known:false unconditionally — it now names the coverage range up front instead of contradicting the paragraph below it.
- D1c the handleAnswerStatus degrade list now includes the unwritable and no-rewrite-mark cases.
- D3 crypto.ts's write-ordering warning named only keys.ts as its dependent; it now names both mechanisms AND records that the ordering is an inference from NTFS behaviour rather than a documented platform guarantee.
- D5 `generation?: string` is now `generation: string | null` — required, explicitly nullable. Runtime leniency unchanged (a missing generation still degrades, never throws); the strict type is what stops a silent omission. The degrade-reason branch handles undefined as well as null, so an untyped harness caller reads the same message.

STILL OPEN:
- D6 wall-clock regression re-opens the published window over PRUNED records, so recordsSinceMs's stated invariant is false: prune at t0+25h drops a record, the clock steps back, recordsSinceMs = max(t0, now-24h) covers it again while get() returns null. Reproduced by tmp/attempt-prune-clock-probe.ts (4/4) and independently by Sol with the real store and handler.
- D2 the four-place duplication of the coverage semantics is unaddressed; /simplify is assessing whether the fix is editorial (types.ts canonical, pointers elsewhere) or structural (drift made detectable).
- D4 keys.ts still has no back-reference to ATTEMPT-WITNESS; the link remains one-way.
- D7 the client still decodes AnswerStatusResponse.bridgeStartedMs without reading it; /simplify is judging consume-vs-annotate.

D6 shares its root with #21/S1 — Date.now() treated as monotonic — and all of them should be fixed together with a monotonic anchor, not patched separately.
